import CoreLog.QpThree
# K4 toy province: execution provenance for the `ℚ_[3]` logarithm
**This file is a toy province for task K4, and nothing more.** The algorithm formalised here is the
partial-sum algorithm of the p-adic logarithm on `ℚ_[3]`: the `n`-th step is the finite sum
`∑_{k<n} (-1)^k (x-1)^{k+1}/(k+1)`. It is **not** the η-algorithm of IUT. Nothing in this file
constructs a Θ-link, an `Ism`, or Corollary 3.12; nothing here touches any object of the external
`iut` interfaces audited in `handoffs/core-backward-2026-10-23/M3/`, and no claim is made about
them.
**The point is type discipline, not new mathematics.** The M3 audit found that in those 11
interfaces an output is a bare structure field (`EtaAlg.out`), while `realisation` only says *where*
outputs land; none of them requires an output to be *produced by a legal execution*. This file is
the smallest honest counter-model of that gap on a concrete complete field:
* `LegalExecution` carries the input, the algorithm's trace **by definitional equality**
(`steps_eq : steps = algorithmRun input`), the value, and a convergence proof *for that trace*.
A constant or otherwise chosen sequence cannot be smuggled in, because the trace field is pinned
to the algorithm rather than merely constrained.
* `value_eq_localLog` derives the value from convergence together with the trace equation, so
provenance *determines* the value (`value_unique`).
* `value_mem_logImage` is a *consequence* here, not a hypothesis: the value lies in the principal
unit log image because it is the limit of this algorithm at this input. In the audited interfaces
the analogous statement (`realisation`) is a field, i.e. a landing condition; that is exactly the
difference this toy province is built to exhibit.
**What this toy province does not establish.** It says nothing about the IUT η-algorithm, Θ-links,
`Ism`, Corollary 3.12, Galois actions, adelic/hull conditions, localisation, or degree comparisons.
It shows that a provenance-typed interface *can* be written on one concrete example and that such an
interface determines its value; it does **not** show that any IUT interface has been recast in that
form, and it is not evidence for or against any IUT claim.
Series conventions: the term is the one already used by `CoreTransport.localLog` and by
`PadicLogVolume.logTerm`; convergence on principal units is the existing
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable` / `principal_unit_log_hasSum` result, quoted rather than
re-proved.
namespace ExecutionProvenance
noncomputable section
open Filter Topology
/-- **The genuine finite algorithm.** The `n`-th partial sum of the logarithm series at `x`, with
the same term `(-1)^k (x-1)^(k+1)/(k+1)` as `CoreTransport.localLog`.
This is the p-adic logarithm's partial-sum algorithm on `ℚ_[3]`, *not* the η-algorithm of IUT; see
the module docstring. It is a plain definition, so any `LegalExecution` trace is bound to it by
definitional equality (`rfl`), not by a hypothesis. -/
def algorithmRun (x : ℚ_[3]) (n : ℕ) : ℚ_[3] :=
/-- The algorithm's `n`-th partial sum *is* the `n`-th partial sum of the existing series term,
definitionally. This is the bridge that lets the trace equation below reach the library's
convergence theorem; it adds no content of its own. -/
theorem algorithmRun_eq_partialSums (x : ℚ_[3]) :
algorithmRun x = fun n : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm x k := by
funext n
rfl
/-- **Definition-level identification of the two literal series.** `CoreTransport.localLog` and
`PadicLogVolume.padicLog` are the same series, written twice; this records that fact in the open by
unfolding both definitions. It is not mathematical content, and no later claim rests on the two
being secretly different objects.
This is the same statement as `DelegatedLogBridge.localLog_eq_padicLog`. It is repeated here — with
its companion `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` — only because that module is not part of the
`CoreTransport` library target (`lake build DelegatedLogBridge` fails with ``unknown target
`DelegatedLogBridge` ``) and no `DelegatedLogBridge.olean` exists, so importing it would make this
file depend on an artifact Lake does not produce. -/
theorem localLog_eq_padicLog (x : ℚ_[3]) :
CoreTransport.localLog x = PadicLogVolume.padicLog x := by
unfold CoreTransport.localLog PadicLogVolume.padicLog PadicLogVolume.logTerm
rfl
/-- **The existing convergence result, quoted.** For `‖x - 1‖ < 1` the series sums to
`CoreTransport.localLog x`; the proof goes through `CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable`, so it
depends on the genuine p-adic convergence argument and not on `tsum`'s totalised default. -/
theorem hasSum_logTerm_localLog {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
HasSum (PadicLogVolume.logTerm x) (CoreTransport.localLog x) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog x]
exact CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum hx
/-- **Execution provenance: a value that exists only together with a named algorithm and a proof
that it is that algorithm's limit.**
The intended reading of each field:
* `input`, `mem` — the input and the domain condition the algorithm needs;
* `steps`, `steps_eq` — the trace *is* `algorithmRun input`, by definitional equality. This field is
the whole point: without it a trace could be any sequence, e.g. a constant one, and the
convergence field below would then certify an arbitrary value;
* `value`, `converges` — the limit of that trace.
Because `steps` is pinned to `algorithmRun input`, the pair `(value, converges)` cannot be chosen
freely: `value_eq_localLog` forces `value = CoreTransport.localLog input`. Nothing here refers to
IUT; see the module docstring. -/
structure LegalExecution where
/-- The input of the execution. -/
input : ℚ_[3]
/-- The input lies in the principal-unit domain of the logarithm series. -/
mem : ‖input - 1‖ < 1
/-- The trace of the execution, step by step. -/
steps : ℕ → ℚ_[3]
/-- The trace **is** the algorithm, by definitional equality: no other sequence is allowed. -/
steps_eq : steps = algorithmRun input
/-- The value of the execution. -/
value : ℚ_[3]
/-- That value is the limit of that trace. -/
converges : Filter.Tendsto steps Filter.atTop (𝓝 value)
/-- **Provenance determines the value.** The value of a legal execution is the limit of the
algorithm's partial sums at its input; the limit is unique, so it equals
`CoreTransport.localLog input`. The three ingredients are `converges` (the limit statement),
`steps_eq` (the trace is the algorithm) and `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` (the library's convergence
result); the conclusion is `tendsto_nhds_unique` of the two.
Note which way the dependency runs: the value is *forced* by the trace, and the trace is forced by
the algorithm. The proof cannot be reproduced with a constant trace, because then `steps_eq` would
have to prove a constant sequence equal to `algorithmRun input`. -/
theorem value_eq_localLog (e : LegalExecution) : e.value = CoreTransport.localLog e.input := by
-- the trace, being the algorithm, converges to the value the structure records
have hrun : Tendsto (algorithmRun e.input) Filter.atTop (𝓝 e.value) := by
rw [← e.steps_eq]
exact e.converges
have hsteps : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm e.input k)
Filter.atTop (𝓝 e.value) := by
simpa only [algorithmRun_eq_partialSums] using hrun
-- the same partial sums converge to `localLog`, by the existing Q_3 theorem
have hlog : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm e.input k)
Filter.atTop (𝓝 (CoreTransport.localLog e.input)) :=
(hasSum_logTerm_localLog e.mem).tendsto_sum_nat
exact tendsto_nhds_unique hsteps hlog
/-- **Provenance determines the value**, as a statement about two executions: same input, hence same
value. No further data is consulted — not the chosen trace, not the chosen value, not any region the
value might land in. -/
theorem value_unique {e₁ e₂ : LegalExecution} (h : e₁.input = e₂.input) :
e₁.value = e₂.value := by
rw [value_eq_localLog e₁, value_eq_localLog e₂, h]
/-- **Anti-degeneracy, as a consequence rather than a condition.** The value of a legal execution
lies in the principal-unit log image `CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]`.
This is deliberately *not* an assumption of `LegalExecution`: it follows from `value_eq_localLog`,
i.e. from the fact that the value is the algorithm's limit. It is recorded to make the contrast with
the audited interfaces explicit — there, the analogous statement is a structure field
(`EtaAlg.realisation`), i.e. a landing condition, and a landing condition alone can never determine
a value. See `logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall` for how weak that condition is. -/
theorem value_mem_logImage (e : LegalExecution) : e.value ∈ CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3] :=
⟨e.input, e.mem, (value_eq_localLog e).symm⟩
/-- **Why a landing condition cannot replace provenance.** The principal-unit log image of `ℚ_[3]`
is the whole closed ball of radius `‖3‖ = 1/3`, not a single point: membership in it is satisfied by
an entire ball of values, so it can never pin down which value an execution produced.
This is the same statement as `DelegatedLogBridge.logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall`, obtained here from
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_image` through the definition-level identification of the two literal
series (`localLog_eq_padicLog`). -/
theorem logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall :
CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3] = {y : ℚ_[3] | ‖y‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹} := by
unfold CoreTransport.logImage
rw [show (CoreTransport.localLog : ℚ_[3] → ℚ_[3]) = PadicLogVolume.padicLog from
funext localLog_eq_padicLog]
exact CoreLog.principal_unit_log_image
theorem norm_four_sub_one : ‖(4 : ℚ_[3]) - 1‖ < 1 := by
have h : (4 : ℚ_[3]) - 1 = 3 := by norm_num
rw [h]
exact CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
/-- **Non-vacuity.** A concrete legal execution at the input `4 : ℚ_[3]`, with the genuine trace
`algorithmRun 4` and the value it forces. Every field is discharged by an actual proof: `mem` by
`norm_four_sub_one`, `steps_eq` by `rfl` (definitional equality with the algorithm), `converges` by
the existing convergence theorem composed with `algorithmRun_eq_partialSums`. -/
def witnessFour : LegalExecution where
input := 4
mem := norm_four_sub_one
steps := algorithmRun 4
steps_eq := rfl
value := CoreTransport.localLog 4
converges := by
rw [algorithmRun_eq_partialSums]
exact (hasSum_logTerm_localLog norm_four_sub_one).tendsto_sum_nat
/-- The non-vacuity witness, at the type `LegalExecution` itself: the structure is inhabited by an
actual execution at the input `4`. -/
example : LegalExecution := witnessFour
end
end ExecutionProvenance

#print axioms ExecutionProvenance.algorithmRun_eq_partialSums

#print axioms ExecutionProvenance.hasSum_logTerm_localLog
#print axioms ExecutionProvenance.value_eq_localLog
#print axioms ExecutionProvenance.value_unique
#print axioms ExecutionProvenance.value_mem_logImage
#print axioms ExecutionProvenance.logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall

target_lines: import CoreTransport.Basic
import CoreLog.QpThree
# W1 toy province: the reading is invariant under a change of presentation, the partial reading is not
**This file is a toy province for task W1 of the backward plan, and nothing more.** It formalises one
shape and only that shape: *a reading of an object that is determined only up to isomorphism must be
proved independent of the chosen presentation, and a partial reading of the same object is not
invariant.* Concretely, the presentation here is the enumeration of an algorithm's steps
(`Equiv.Perm ℕ`), the reading is the unconditional series sum (`tsum`), and the partial reading is the
finite partial sum (`∑ k ∈ Finset.range n`).
**Why the obligation exists.** `research/core-backward-2026-10-23/h1-decision.md`, §结论一′, quotes
the source (txt lines 8869–8873) defining `n,◦HT^{D-Θ±ellNF}` as the Hodge theater "determined, **up to
isomorphism**, by the various `n,m`-theaters". An object determined only up to isomorphism has no
canonical presentation, so a reading built on it must be proved invariant under a change of
presentation; otherwise the reading lives on a chosen presentation and not on the object. The same
decision records that none of the 11 audited interfaces (`handoffs/core-backward-2026-10-23/M3/`)
carries such an invariance (F3 is false for all of them), so W1 cannot inherit the invariance from the
interfaces and has to prove it.
**This is an analogue of Ind1–Ind3, not Ind1–Ind3.** The permutation group `Equiv.Perm ℕ` stands in
for the change of presentation and `tsum` stands in for the reading; Ind1–Ind3 themselves concern
indeterminacies of the Θ-link. Nothing below constructs a Θ-link, an `Ism`, a prime-strip, a
Frobenioid, a Hodge theater, coricity, or a Galois action, and no claim is made about any of them.
**The substance of the file is item 4, the anti-degeneracy statement.** Invariance of an unconditional
sum under a bijective reindexing is a general topological fact, quoted here from Mathlib
(`Equiv.hasSum_iff`) on top of the existing convergence theorem
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum`; convergence is not re-proved. What is *not* general, and is proved
below with a concrete witness, is that the finite partial reading of the same algorithm is **not**
invariant — so "the reading" cannot be taken to be a partial sum. The witness is explicit: at
`x = 4 : ℚ_[3]` the third term of the series is `9` and the first is `3`; reordering the enumeration so
that step 2 is executed first, and stopping after one step, gives `9` against `3` for the identity
enumeration. The two are separated by their norms, `‖9‖ = 1/9 ≠ 1/3 = ‖3‖`, so the failure does not
depend on any totalised value of a divergent series.
**What this file does not establish.** It does not formalise Ind1–Ind3, the Θ-link, `(n,◦)`, or any
other H1 object; it does not show that the invariance obligation of §结论一′ is discharged for the real
object, only that its *shape* — invariant reading, non-invariant partial reading — is consistent and
provable on one concrete complete field. It is not evidence for or against any IUT claim.
Series conventions: the term is the one already used by `CoreTransport.localLog` and by
`PadicLogVolume.logTerm`. `CoreTransport.localLog` and `PadicLogVolume.padicLog` are the same series
written twice (`localLog_eq_padicLog`, by unfolding both definitions), exactly as in
`ExecutionProvenance.lean`; that identification is repeated here only so that this file depends on
`CoreTransport.Basic` and `CoreLog.QpThree` alone.
namespace ReadingInvariance
noncomputable section
open Filter Topology
/-! ## The two presentations, and the reading -/
/-- `CoreTransport.localLog` and `PadicLogVolume.padicLog` are the same series, written twice; this
records that in the open by unfolding both definitions. It carries no mathematical content of its own,
and no later claim rests on the two being secretly different objects. -/
theorem localLog_eq_padicLog (x : ℚ_[3]) :
CoreTransport.localLog x = PadicLogVolume.padicLog x := by
unfold CoreTransport.localLog PadicLogVolume.padicLog PadicLogVolume.logTerm
rfl
/-- **The existing convergence result, quoted rather than re-proved.** For `‖x - 1‖ < 1` the logarithm
series sums to `CoreTransport.localLog x`; the proof goes through
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable`, i.e. through the genuine p-adic convergence argument and not
through `tsum`'s totalised default. -/
theorem hasSum_logTerm_localLog {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
HasSum (PadicLogVolume.logTerm x) (CoreTransport.localLog x) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog x]
exact CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum hx
/-- **The algorithm run in the order given by `σ`.** The permutation `σ` *is* the presentation: it says
in which order the steps of the algorithm are executed. With `σ = 1` this is the step order
`0, 1, 2, …`. This is the toy stand-in for "the presentation is fixed only up to isomorphism"; see the
module docstring for the exact sense in which it is an analogue only. -/
def partialSumAlong (σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (x : ℚ_[3]) (n : ℕ) : ℚ_[3] :=
∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm x (σ k)
/-- The one-step partial sum is exactly the term the presentation picks first. -/
theorem partialSumAlong_one (σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (x : ℚ_[3]) :
partialSumAlong σ x 1 = PadicLogVolume.logTerm x (σ 0) := by
rw [partialSumAlong, Finset.sum_range_one]
/-- **The reading is the same for every enumeration.** For `‖x - 1‖ < 1`, the sum of the algorithm's
terms taken in the order given by any permutation `σ` still has sum `CoreTransport.localLog x`.
The only input beyond the quoted convergence theorem is that an unconditionally convergent sum is
invariant under a bijective reindexing of its terms; here that is `Equiv.hasSum_iff`
(`HasSum (f ∘ e) a ↔ HasSum f a`, the additive form of `Equiv.hasProd_iff` in
`Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/Basic.lean`). Convergence is not re-proved. -/
theorem hasSum_perm (σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ) {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
HasSum (fun n => PadicLogVolume.logTerm x (σ n)) (CoreTransport.localLog x) := by
have h := (Equiv.hasSum_iff (f := fun k => PadicLogVolume.logTerm x k) σ).mpr
(hasSum_logTerm_localLog hx)
simpa only [Function.comp_def] using h
/-- **Two presentations, one reading.** The two sides are kept literally as `tsum`s over the two
enumerations, so the statement is about the presentations and not about `CoreTransport.localLog` by
construction. -/
theorem reading_independent_of_enumeration (σ τ : Equiv.Perm ℕ) {x : ℚ_[3]}
(∑' n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm x (σ n)) = (∑' n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm x (τ n)) := by
rw [(hasSum_perm σ hx).tsum_eq, (hasSum_perm τ hx).tsum_eq]
/-! ## Anti-degeneracy: the partial reading is not invariant -/
/-- The first term of the series at `x = 4 : ℚ_[3]` is `3`. -/
theorem logTerm_four_zero : PadicLogVolume.logTerm (4 : ℚ_[3]) 0 = 3 := by
rw [PadicLogVolume.logTerm_zero]
norm_num
/-- The third term of the series at `x = 4 : ℚ_[3]` is `9`: `(-1)^2 (4-1)^3 / 3 = 27/3 = 9`. -/
theorem logTerm_four_two : PadicLogVolume.logTerm (4 : ℚ_[3]) 2 = 9 := by
unfold PadicLogVolume.logTerm
norm_num
/-- `‖9‖ = 1/9` in `ℚ_[3]`, from `‖3‖ = 1/3` and `9 = 3 ^ 2`. This is the invariant used to separate
the two partial sums of `partialSum_not_invariant`. -/
theorem norm_nine : ‖(9 : ℚ_[3])‖ = (9 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
have h : (9 : ℚ_[3]) = 3 ^ 2 := by norm_num
rw [h, norm_pow, CoreLog.norm_three]
norm_num
/-- **The partial reading is not invariant.** A concrete failure, not a negated universal: take `σ`
to be the transposition `0 ↔ 2` and stop after `n = 1` step. The transposition executes step `2` at
position `0` of the trace, so the one-step partial sum is the third term `9`; the identity presentation
stopped after one step gives the first term `3`. The two are separated by their norms,
This is the point of the file: it is what forbids taking "the reading" to be a partial sum. Note that
the failure is produced by a reordering *within* the same algorithm at the same input `x = 4`, so the
two values differ in a way that the enumeration alone decides. -/
theorem partialSum_not_invariant :
∃ (σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (n : ℕ),
partialSumAlong σ (4 : ℚ_[3]) n ≠
partialSumAlong (1 : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (4 : ℚ_[3]) n := by
refine ⟨Equiv.swap 0 2, 1, ?_⟩
have hσ : partialSumAlong (Equiv.swap 0 2) (4 : ℚ_[3]) 1 = (9 : ℚ_[3]) := by
rw [partialSumAlong_one, Equiv.swap_apply_left, logTerm_four_two]
have hid : partialSumAlong (1 : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (4 : ℚ_[3]) 1 = (3 : ℚ_[3]) := by
rw [partialSumAlong_one]
simpa using logTerm_four_zero
rw [hσ, hid]
intro h
have hnorm : (9 : ℝ)⁻¹ = (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
rw [← norm_nine, ← CoreLog.norm_three, h]
norm_num at hnorm
end
end ReadingInvariance
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.localLog_eq_padicLog
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.hasSum_logTerm_localLog
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.partialSumAlong
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.partialSumAlong_one
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.hasSum_perm
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.reading_independent_of_enumeration
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.logTerm_four_zero
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.logTerm_four_two
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.norm_nine
#print axioms ReadingInvariance.partialSum_not_invariant

import CoreLog.QpThree
# W2 toy province: execution provenance for a local-global *collection*, not for a single element
**This file is a toy province for task W2 of the backward plan, and nothing more.** K4
(`candidates/core-transport/ExecutionProvenance.lean`) put execution provenance on a *single*
element: an object whose value exists only together with a named algorithm and a proof that the value
is that algorithm's limit. This file lifts that type from one element to a **collection** and proves
that provenance determines the reading of the whole collection, not merely of one piece.
**Why a collection and not an element.** `research/core-backward-2026-10-23/h1-decision.md`, §结论二,
quotes the source (txt lines 8607–8629) defining the category `⊼fQ₂` of "local-global collections" and
its `⊼`-version `⊼fQ₁`, and the "local-global `⊼`-collections" `⊼lc₁` of txt 8566–8571; the objects
there consist of local pieces indexed by the places of a number field, one global object, and
localisation morphisms relating them. This file models that **shape at the set level only**, with
`Fin n` in place of the set of places:
* `localInput v`, `mem v` — the `n` local inputs, each in the principal-unit domain;
* `localSteps v`, `steps_eq v` — each local piece is **produced** by the algorithm, by definitional
equality with `algorithmRun (localInput v)`, exactly as in K4;
* `localValue v`, `converges v` — each local reading is the limit of that local trace;
* `globalValue`, `localization` — one global reading, related to the local readings.
**The `localization` field is a toy stand-in, and a degenerate one.** In the source it is a family of
localisation *morphisms* between genuinely different objects, with a nontrivial compatibility
structure. Here it is the single equation `globalValue = localValue v` for every `v`: the global
reading is *the common local reading*. That is the crudest possible stand-in for localisation and it
is stated as such — it captures only the one feature this file needs, namely that the global reading is
tied to the local ones rather than being free. It is **not** IUT's localisation, and no claim below is
about IUT's localisation.
**What is proved.**
* `localValue_determined` — componentwise, each local reading is `CoreTransport.localLog` of its own
input, from `converges`, `steps_eq` and the quoted convergence theorem, by uniqueness of limits.
* `localValues_determined` — the whole local reading *function* is determined, not one component.
* `globalValue_determined_at` / `globalValue_determined` — the global reading is likewise fixed, at an
arbitrary index and (as required) at the index `0`.
* `both_readings_unique` — two collections with the same local inputs have the same local reading
function and the same global reading: provenance ties the reading to the input data alone.
* `localValue_mem_logImage`, `landing_of_provenance` — every local reading lies in the principal-unit
log image `CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]`. This is a **consequence**, not a field: the whole contrast
of this file is that landing is derived from provenance, never assumed in its place.
**The anti-degeneracy statement, stated precisely.** What is proved is the *preferred* form:
`landing_does_not_determine_global` exhibits **two collections with the same `n`** (namely `n = 1`),
each of whose local readings lies in `CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]` — so both satisfy the landing
predicate in the strongest available sense, as a theorem about them — whose **global readings differ**.
`landing_does_not_determine_global_nontrivial` repeats the separation with two inputs that are both
different from `1`, so the failure is not an artefact of the trivial input.
The fallback offered in the task statement — one collection with `n = 1` against one with `n = 2` —
was **not needed**: the toy's `localization` field does *not* make the same-`n` statement impossible.
The field forces the global reading to equal a local one, and two collections with `n = 1` may still
have different local readings, hence different global readings; nothing in `localization` compares two
*different* collections. What the toy does make impossible is the superficially stronger statement
"same local readings, different global reading": `both_readings_unique` proves that two collections
with the same `localInput` have the same `globalValue`, so a separation can only be produced by data
the landing predicate does not see — the inputs. That is exactly the honest content: the landing
predicate is a property of values alone, and it is satisfied by collections whose readings are
different values, while provenance is a property of the trace and pins the reading.
**Not a circularity, and where the work is.** Nothing above assumes the conclusion: `localValue` and
`globalValue` are arbitrary fields of the structure, and the theorems *derive* their values from
`steps_eq` (definitional equality with the algorithm) plus `converges`. The separation lemmas are
concrete computations on `ℚ_[3]` (`localLog 4 ≠ 0`, `localLog 4 ≠ localLog (-2)`), obtained from the
existing rearrangement `PadicLogVolume.padicLog_one_add` and its remainder estimate
`PadicLogVolume.norm_logRem_le` — no new analysis of the logarithm is performed here.
**What this toy province does not establish.** It says nothing about the IUT η-algorithm, Θ-links,
`Ism`, Corollary 3.12, prime-strips, Frobenioids, Hodge theaters, Galois actions, adelic/hull
conditions, the category `⊼fQ₂`, its `⊼`-version `⊼fQ₁`, or the formal quotient `⊼fQ₂ modulo ⊼fQ₁` of
§结论二. `Fin n` is a set of indices, not a set of places; `localization` is one equation, not a family
of morphisms; and the logarithm series on `ℚ_[3]` is not the η-algorithm. The file shows that a
provenance-typed *collection* can be written and that it determines its own reading while a landing
predicate does not; it is not evidence for or against any IUT claim.
**Why the two quoted lemmas are re-derived here.** `ExecutionProvenance.lean` is not a target of the
Lake library `CoreTransport` (`lakefile.lean` declares only `lean_lib CoreTransport`), so no
`ExecutionProvenance.olean` is produced and `import ExecutionProvenance` is not available; the file was
checked as a standalone module. The same holds for `ReadingInvariance.lean`. Accordingly this file
re-states `algorithmRun` and re-derives `localLog_eq_padicLog` and `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` locally,
exactly as K4 and W1 each did, so that it depends on `CoreTransport.Basic` and `CoreLog.QpThree` alone.
The re-derivation is an identification of two literal series by unfolding both definitions; it adds no
mathematical content, and no claim rests on the two being secretly different objects.
Series conventions: the term is the one already used by `CoreTransport.localLog` and by
`PadicLogVolume.logTerm`; convergence on principal units is the existing
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum`, quoted rather than re-proved.
namespace CollectionProvenance
noncomputable section
open Filter Topology
/-! ## The algorithm, and the quoted convergence theorem -/
/-- **The genuine finite algorithm, re-stated.** The `n`-th partial sum of the logarithm series at
`x`, with the same term `(-1)^k (x-1)^(k+1)/(k+1)` as `CoreTransport.localLog`.
This is a re-statement of `ExecutionProvenance.algorithmRun`, not a new algorithm: the latter's module
is not a target of the Lake library, so it has no compiled interface to import (see the module
docstring). As in that file, this is the p-adic logarithm's partial-sum algorithm on `ℚ_[3]`, *not* the
η-algorithm of IUT. Being a plain definition, it binds any trace in `LocalGlobalCollection` by
definitional equality (`rfl`), not by a hypothesis. -/
def algorithmRun (x : ℚ_[3]) (n : ℕ) : ℚ_[3] :=
/-- The algorithm's `n`-th partial sum *is* the `n`-th partial sum of the existing series term,
definitionally. This is the bridge from the trace equation to the library's convergence theorem; it
adds no content of its own. -/
theorem algorithmRun_eq_partialSums (x : ℚ_[3]) :
algorithmRun x = fun n : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm x k := by
funext n
rfl
/-- `CoreTransport.localLog` and `PadicLogVolume.padicLog` are the same series, written twice; this
records that in the open by unfolding both definitions. Re-derived here for the same reason as
`algorithmRun`: no compiled interface of the K4 module is available. It carries no mathematical
content of its own. -/
theorem localLog_eq_padicLog (x : ℚ_[3]) :
CoreTransport.localLog x = PadicLogVolume.padicLog x := by
unfold CoreTransport.localLog PadicLogVolume.padicLog PadicLogVolume.logTerm
rfl
/-- **The existing convergence result, quoted.** For `‖x - 1‖ < 1` the series sums to
`CoreTransport.localLog x`; the proof goes through `CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable`, so it
depends on the genuine p-adic convergence argument and not on `tsum`'s totalised default. -/
theorem hasSum_logTerm_localLog {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
HasSum (PadicLogVolume.logTerm x) (CoreTransport.localLog x) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog x]
exact CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum hx
/-! ## The local-global collection -/
-- `localSteps` and `localValue` are families *labelled* by the index: the binder `v` is part of the
-- declared shape even where the type on the right does not consume it (`∀ v, ℕ → ℚ_[3]` and
-- `∀ v, ℚ_[3]`). The unused-variable linter is therefore off around the structure below, so that the
-- fields keep exactly the names and binder shapes stated in the task; it is switched back on at once.
set_option linter.unusedVariables false
/-- **A local-global collection with execution provenance at every local piece, and one global
reading.**
This is the set-level shape of `⊼lc-gl` as recorded in `h1-decision.md`, §结论二 (local objects, one
global object, localisation between them), with `Fin n` in place of the places of a number field. The
intended reading of each field:
* `localInput`, `mem` — the `n` local inputs, each in the principal-unit domain of the logarithm;
* `localSteps`, `steps_eq` — the local trace **is** `algorithmRun (localInput v)`, by definitional
equality. As in K4 this is the field that carries provenance: without it a trace could be any
sequence, e.g. a constant one, and `converges` would then certify an arbitrary value;
* `localValue`, `converges` — each local reading is the limit of that local trace;
* `globalValue`, `localization` — one global reading, tied to the local ones by
`globalValue = localValue v` for all `v`.
**The `localization` field is a toy stand-in.** In the source the localisation data are morphisms
between genuinely different objects with a compatibility structure; here it is the single equation
"the global reading is the common local reading", the crudest relation of the required shape. It is not
IUT's localisation. See the module docstring.
Nothing here mentions IUT, and no field is a landing condition: `localValue` lies in
`CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]` only as a *theorem* (`localValue_mem_logImage`). -/
structure LocalGlobalCollection (n : ℕ) where
/-- The `n` local inputs. -/
localInput : Fin n → ℚ_[3]
/-- Each local input lies in the principal-unit domain of the logarithm series. -/
mem : ∀ v, ‖localInput v - 1‖ < 1
/-- The trace of the local execution at each index, step by step. -/
localSteps : ∀ v, ℕ → ℚ_[3]
/-- Each local trace **is** the algorithm at that local input, by definitional equality. -/
steps_eq : ∀ v, localSteps v = algorithmRun (localInput v)
/-- The local reading at each index. -/
localValue : ∀ v, ℚ_[3]
/-- Each local reading is the limit of the corresponding local trace. -/
converges : ∀ v, Filter.Tendsto (localSteps v) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (localValue v))
/-- The global reading. -/
globalValue : ℚ_[3]
/-- **Toy localisation**: the global reading is the common local reading. Not IUT's localisation. -/
localization : ∀ v, globalValue = localValue v
set_option linter.unusedVariables true
/-- The provenance field, read as a single statement: the collection's trace function *is* the
algorithm applied to the collection's input function. `funext` of `steps_eq`, no more. -/
theorem localSteps_eq_algorithm (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) :
c.localSteps = fun v => algorithmRun (c.localInput v) :=
funext c.steps_eq
/-! ## Provenance determines the reading -/
/-- **Provenance determines each local reading.** The local reading at `v` is the limit of the local
trace; the trace is the algorithm at `localInput v`; the algorithm's partial sums converge to
`CoreTransport.localLog (localInput v)` by the quoted theorem; the limit is unique.
The three ingredients are `converges v` (the limit statement), `steps_eq v` (the trace is the
algorithm) and `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` (the library's convergence theorem). Which way the dependency
runs matters: the reading is *forced* by the trace, and the trace is forced by the algorithm and the
input. The proof cannot be reproduced with a constant trace, because `steps_eq v` would then have to
prove a constant sequence equal to `algorithmRun (c.localInput v)`. -/
theorem localValue_determined (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) (v : Fin n) :
c.localValue v = CoreTransport.localLog (c.localInput v) := by
-- the trace, being the algorithm, converges to the local reading the structure records
have hrun : Tendsto (algorithmRun (c.localInput v)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (c.localValue v)) := by
rw [← c.steps_eq v]
exact c.converges v
have hsteps : Tendsto
(fun m : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, PadicLogVolume.logTerm (c.localInput v) k)
Filter.atTop (𝓝 (c.localValue v)) := by
simpa only [algorithmRun_eq_partialSums] using hrun
-- the same partial sums converge to `localLog`, by the existing Q_3 theorem
have hlog : Tendsto
(fun m : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, PadicLogVolume.logTerm (c.localInput v) k)
Filter.atTop (𝓝 (CoreTransport.localLog (c.localInput v))) :=
(hasSum_logTerm_localLog (c.mem v)).tendsto_sum_nat
exact tendsto_nhds_unique hsteps hlog
/-- **Provenance determines the whole local reading function**, not one component: the reading is
`CoreTransport.localLog` composed with the collection's input function. -/
theorem localValues_determined (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) :
c.localValue = fun v => CoreTransport.localLog (c.localInput v) :=
funext fun v => localValue_determined c v
/-- **Provenance determines the global reading, at any chosen index.** The toy localisation identifies
the global reading with the local one, and the local one is already forced. -/
theorem globalValue_determined_at (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) (v : Fin n) :
c.globalValue = CoreTransport.localLog (c.localInput v) := by
rw [c.localization v, localValue_determined c v]
/-- **Provenance determines the global reading**, stated for `n ≥ 1` in the form `Fin (n + 1)`, with
the index `0` used for the toy localisation.
The `Fin (n + 1)` shape is a choice, made to state the requirement without an extra
`[NeZero n]`-style hypothesis: `0 : Fin (n + 1)` needs no side condition. The general form
`globalValue_determined_at` is stronger — it holds at *every* index and for every `n` — and this
theorem is its specialisation. -/
theorem globalValue_determined {n : ℕ} (c : LocalGlobalCollection (n + 1)) :
c.globalValue = CoreTransport.localLog (c.localInput 0) :=
globalValue_determined_at c 0
/-- **Two collections with the same inputs have the same reading**, local function and global value
alike. This is the collection-level form of K4's `value_unique`, and it is what fixes the boundary of
the anti-degeneracy statements below: a separation between two readings can only come from data the
provenance-typed reading actually consumes, namely the inputs. -/
theorem both_readings_unique {n : ℕ} {c₁ c₂ : LocalGlobalCollection n}
(h : c₁.localInput = c₂.localInput) (v : Fin n) :
c₁.localValue = c₂.localValue ∧ c₁.globalValue = c₂.globalValue := by
constructor
· funext u
rw [localValue_determined c₁ u, localValue_determined c₂ u, h]
· rw [globalValue_determined_at c₁ v, globalValue_determined_at c₂ v, h]
/-! ## Landing is a consequence of provenance, not a substitute for it -/
/-- **Landing, as a consequence rather than a condition.** Each local reading lies in the
principal-unit log image `CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]`.
This is deliberately *not* a field of `LocalGlobalCollection`: it follows from
`localValue_determined`, i.e. from the fact that the reading is the algorithm's limit at a
principal-unit input. It is recorded to make the contrast with the audited interfaces explicit — there
the analogous statement is a structure field (`EtaAlg.realisation`), i.e. a landing condition, and a
landing condition alone can never determine a value. See `logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall` for how weak that
condition is. -/
theorem localValue_mem_logImage (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) (v : Fin n) :
c.localValue v ∈ CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3] :=
⟨c.localInput v, c.mem v, (localValue_determined c v).symm⟩
/-- **The landing predicate on a collection**: every local reading lies in the log image. This is the
collection-level analogue of a `realisation` field; here it is a predicate, proved of every collection
by `landing_of_provenance`. -/
def SatisfiesLanding {n : ℕ} (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) : Prop :=
∀ v, c.localValue v ∈ CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]
/-- **Every collection satisfies the landing predicate**, as a theorem. So the predicate constrains
nothing about the readings — which is the point of the two separation statements below. -/
theorem landing_of_provenance (c : LocalGlobalCollection n) : SatisfiesLanding c :=
fun v => localValue_mem_logImage c v
/-- **Why a landing condition cannot replace provenance.** The principal-unit log image of `ℚ_[3]` is
the whole closed ball of radius `‖3‖ = 1/3`, not a single point: membership in it is satisfied by an
entire ball of values, so it can never pin down which value an execution produced.
This is the same statement as in K4 and in `DelegatedLogBridge`, obtained here from
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_image` through the definition-level identification of the two literal
series (`localLog_eq_padicLog`). -/
theorem logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall :
CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3] = {y : ℚ_[3] | ‖y‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹} := by
unfold CoreTransport.logImage
rw [show (CoreTransport.localLog : ℚ_[3] → ℚ_[3]) = PadicLogVolume.padicLog from
funext localLog_eq_padicLog]
exact CoreLog.principal_unit_log_image
/-! ## Concrete computations used to separate two readings -/
theorem norm_four_sub_one : ‖(4 : ℚ_[3]) - 1‖ < 1 := by
have h : (4 : ℚ_[3]) - 1 = 3 := by norm_num
rw [h]
exact CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
theorem norm_neg_two_sub_one : ‖(-2 : ℚ_[3]) - 1‖ < 1 := by
have h : (-2 : ℚ_[3]) - 1 = -3 := by norm_num
rw [h, norm_neg]
exact CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
/-- `1` is a principal unit of `ℚ_[3]`: `‖1 - 1‖ = 0 < 1`. -/
theorem norm_one_sub_one : ‖(1 : ℚ_[3]) - 1‖ < 1 := by
have h : (1 : ℚ_[3]) - 1 = 0 := by norm_num
rw [h, norm_zero]
norm_num
theorem norm_two_Q3 : ‖(2 : ℚ_[3])‖ = 1 :=
PadicLogVolume.norm_two_eq_one (p := 3) (by decide) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one (by decide)
/-- `‖2 * 3‖ = ‖3‖ = 1/3`, so `3` sits inside the ball of radius `‖2p‖` on which the remainder
estimate `PadicLogVolume.norm_logRem_le` applies. -/
theorem norm_two_mul_three : ‖(2 : ℚ_[3]) * 3‖ = (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
rw [norm_mul, norm_two_Q3, one_mul, CoreLog.norm_three]
/-- `‖3‖ ≤ ‖2 * 3‖`, the hypothesis shape required by `PadicLogVolume.norm_logRem_le`. -/
theorem norm_three_le_two_mul_three : ‖(3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ ‖(2 : ℚ_[3]) * 3‖ := by
rw [CoreLog.norm_three, norm_two_mul_three]
/-- **The remainder estimate at `a = 3`.** `‖logRem 3‖ ≤ ‖3‖ * ‖3‖ = 1/9`, from the existing
contraction estimate for the remainder `log (1 + a) - a`. -/
theorem norm_logRem_three_le : ‖PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ (9 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
have h := PadicLogVolume.norm_logRem_le (p := 3) (by decide) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
(a := (3 : ℚ_[3])) norm_three_le_two_mul_three
have h' : ‖PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ * (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
simpa only [Nat.cast_ofNat, CoreLog.norm_three] using h
calc ‖PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ * (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ := h'
_ = (9 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by norm_num
/-- The same estimate at `a = -3`, which is the input `-2 = 1 + (-3)`. -/
theorem norm_logRem_neg_three_le : ‖PadicLogVolume.logRem (-3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ (9 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
have h := PadicLogVolume.norm_logRem_le (p := 3) (by decide) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
(a := (-3 : ℚ_[3])) (by rw [norm_neg]; exact norm_three_le_two_mul_three)
have h' : ‖PadicLogVolume.logRem (-3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ * (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
simpa only [Nat.cast_ofNat, norm_neg, CoreLog.norm_three] using h
calc ‖PadicLogVolume.logRem (-3 : ℚ_[3])‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ * (3 : ℝ)⁻¹ := h'
_ = (9 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by norm_num
/-- `localLog 1 = 0`, since every term of the series at `1` vanishes. -/
theorem localLog_one : CoreTransport.localLog (1 : ℚ_[3]) = 0 := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog]
exact PadicLogVolume.padicLog_one
/-- **`localLog` at `4 = 1 + 3`, split off its linear part**: `log 4 = 3 + logRem 3`, from the
existing rearrangement `PadicLogVolume.padicLog_one_add`. -/
theorem localLog_four :
CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) = 3 + PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3]) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog]
have h4 : (4 : ℚ_[3]) = 1 + 3 := by norm_num
rw [h4]
exact PadicLogVolume.padicLog_one_add (p := 3) (by decide) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
(a := (3 : ℚ_[3])) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
theorem localLog_neg_two :
CoreTransport.localLog (-2 : ℚ_[3]) = -3 + PadicLogVolume.logRem (-3 : ℚ_[3]) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog]
have h2 : (-2 : ℚ_[3]) = 1 + (-3) := by norm_num
rw [h2]
exact PadicLogVolume.padicLog_one_add (p := 3) (by decide) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
(a := (-3 : ℚ_[3])) (by rw [norm_neg]; exact CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one)
/-- **`localLog 4 ≠ 0`.** If it were zero, the remainder `logRem 3 = log 4 - 3` would equal `-3`,
whose norm is `1/3`; but `‖logRem 3‖ ≤ 1/9`. So `localLog 4` is a nonzero point of the log image. -/
theorem localLog_four_ne_zero : CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0 := by
intro h
have h1 : PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3]) = -(3 : ℚ_[3]) := by
rw [localLog_four] at h
linear_combination h
have h3 := norm_logRem_three_le
rw [h1, norm_neg] at h3
exact h3
rw [CoreLog.norm_three] at h2
norm_num at h2
/-- **`localLog 4 ≠ localLog (-2)`.** The two readings differ by `6` up to two remainders of norm at
most `1/9` each, and `‖6‖ = 1/3 > 1/9 + 1/9`. Both inputs are principal units other than `1`, so this
separates two *nontrivial* points of the same log image. -/
theorem localLog_four_ne_localLog_negTwo :
CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) ≠ CoreTransport.localLog (-2 : ℚ_[3]) := by
intro h
have h1 : PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3]) = CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) - 3 := by
rw [localLog_four]
ring
have h2 : PadicLogVolume.logRem (-3 : ℚ_[3]) = CoreTransport.localLog (-2 : ℚ_[3]) + 3 := by

ring
have hdiff : (-6 : ℚ_[3]) =
PadicLogVolume.logRem (3 : ℚ_[3]) - PadicLogVolume.logRem (-3 : ℚ_[3]) := by

ring
rw [hdiff]
refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans ?_
linarith [norm_logRem_three_le, norm_logRem_neg_three_le]
rw [h6, norm_neg, norm_two_mul_three]
rw [hsix] at hnorm
norm_num at hnorm
/-! ## Non-vacuity: three collections -/
/-- **A collection with `n = 1` at the input `4`**, with the genuine trace `algorithmRun 4` and the
reading it forces. Every field is discharged by an actual proof: `mem` by `norm_four_sub_one`,
`steps_eq` by `rfl` (definitional equality with the algorithm), `converges` by the quoted convergence
theorem composed with `algorithmRun_eq_partialSums`, `localization` by `rfl`. -/
def witnessFour : LocalGlobalCollection 1 where
localInput := fun _ => 4
mem := fun _ => norm_four_sub_one
localSteps := fun _ => algorithmRun 4
steps_eq := fun _ => rfl
localValue := fun _ => CoreTransport.localLog 4
converges := fun _ => by
rw [algorithmRun_eq_partialSums]
exact (hasSum_logTerm_localLog norm_four_sub_one).tendsto_sum_nat
globalValue := CoreTransport.localLog 4
localization := fun _ => rfl
/-- **A collection with `n = 1` at the input `-2`**, same shape as `witnessFour`. -/
def witnessNegTwo : LocalGlobalCollection 1 where
localInput := fun _ => -2
mem := fun _ => norm_neg_two_sub_one
localSteps := fun _ => algorithmRun (-2)
steps_eq := fun _ => rfl
localValue := fun _ => CoreTransport.localLog (-2)
converges := fun _ => by
rw [algorithmRun_eq_partialSums]
exact (hasSum_logTerm_localLog norm_neg_two_sub_one).tendsto_sum_nat
globalValue := CoreTransport.localLog (-2)
localization := fun _ => rfl
/-- **A collection with `n = 1` at the input `1`**, whose reading is `log 1 = 0`. -/
def witnessOne : LocalGlobalCollection 1 where
localInput := fun _ => 1
mem := fun _ => norm_one_sub_one
localSteps := fun _ => algorithmRun 1
steps_eq := fun _ => rfl
localValue := fun _ => CoreTransport.localLog 1
converges := fun _ => by
rw [algorithmRun_eq_partialSums]
exact (hasSum_logTerm_localLog norm_one_sub_one).tendsto_sum_nat
globalValue := CoreTransport.localLog 1
localization := fun _ => rfl
/-- Non-vacuity at the type itself: `LocalGlobalCollection 1` is inhabited by an actual collection. -/
example : LocalGlobalCollection 1 := witnessFour
/-! ## Anti-degeneracy: the landing condition does not determine the global reading -/
/-- **The point of the file.** Two collections *with the same `n`* (`n = 1`), each of whose local
readings lands in `CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]` — so both satisfy the landing predicate, by
`landing_of_provenance` — and whose **global readings differ**.
The landing predicate contains no information that could separate them: it says only "the reading lies
in the log image", and both readings do. Provenance, by contrast, separates them immediately, because
it fixes each reading to be the limit of the algorithm at its own input, and the two inputs give
different readings (`localLog_four_ne_zero`, with `localLog 1 = 0`). So a landing condition is not a
substitute for provenance at the level of a collection either.
This is the preferred form of the anti-degeneracy statement, and it is *not* obstructed by the toy's
`localization` field: that field constrains the global reading of a *single* collection against its own
local readings, and says nothing about two different collections. What the toy does rule out is
"same inputs, different readings", which is exactly `both_readings_unique`. -/
theorem landing_does_not_determine_global :
∃ c₁ c₂ : LocalGlobalCollection 1,
SatisfiesLanding c₁ ∧ SatisfiesLanding c₂ ∧ c₁.globalValue ≠ c₂.globalValue := by
refine ⟨witnessFour, witnessOne, landing_of_provenance _, landing_of_provenance _, ?_⟩
show CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) ≠ CoreTransport.localLog (1 : ℚ_[3])
rw [localLog_one]
exact localLog_four_ne_zero
/-- The same separation with **both** inputs nontrivial: `4` and `-2` are principal units different
from `1`, and their readings differ (`localLog_four_ne_localLog_negTwo`). So the failure above is not an
artefact of using the trivial input `1`; it persists between two genuine, nonzero points of the log
image. -/
theorem landing_does_not_determine_global_nontrivial :
∃ c₁ c₂ : LocalGlobalCollection 1,
SatisfiesLanding c₁ ∧ SatisfiesLanding c₂ ∧ c₁.globalValue ≠ c₂.globalValue := by
refine ⟨witnessFour, witnessNegTwo, landing_of_provenance _, landing_of_provenance _, ?_⟩
show CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) ≠ CoreTransport.localLog (-2 : ℚ_[3])
exact localLog_four_ne_localLog_negTwo
end
end CollectionProvenance

import CoreLog.QpThree
# W3 toy province: the `M`-th power is divided back by the logarithm, not by the norm
**This file is a toy province for item 3 of the current goal — the H3 prerequisite of
`research/core-backward-2026-10-23/design-h1-h3.md`, §1′(d) — and nothing more.** It formalises one
shape and only that shape: *a reading that is a logarithm sends the `M`-th power of the object to
`M` times the reading of the object, so dividing back by `M` recovers the original reading; a
reading that is a magnitude instead does not, because dividing by `M` is not what an `M`-th power
does to a magnitude.*
Concretely, on `ℚ_[3]`, with the reading taken on the principal units `‖x - 1‖ < 1`:
* the reading is `CoreTransport.localLog`, the literal logarithm series;
* the stand-in for the "`M`-th tensor power" of the object is the field power `x ^ M`;
* `localLog_pow_eq_smul` and `divide_back` say the reading of `x ^ M` is `M` times the reading of
`x`, hence the reading of `x` is recovered by dividing by `M`;
* `naive_magnitude_divide_back_fails` says the analogous statement is false for the naive magnitude
**Why this shape and not the object itself.** `handoffs/core-backward-2026-10-23/M2/` records three
accounting items that the source leaves open (`normalizations.csv` rows M2-07, M2-12, M2-14, M2-25;
`QUESTIONS.md` Q1–Q3, Q5, Q6), and `design-h1-h3.md` §1′(d) carries them into H3:
* **(M-i) there is no divide-back map in the source.** (Ob4), p.133, txt 8135–8144, and (Ob4-3),
p.134, txt 8185–8189, only *assert* that the confusion between an arithmetic line bundle and its
`M`-th tensor power is harmless. No map from the `M`-th-power reading to the original reading is
constructed there, and no bound and no invariance statement is given.
* **(M-ii) `M` is never valued.** (Ob3-2), p.132, txt 8084–8109, characterises `M` only as the
positive integer with `det^{⊗M}(−)` the `M`-th tensor power, and ties it to `N_E` of
Remark 3.1.1(iv) by a bare "cf." only.
* **(M-iii) two normalizations are used but never written.** (xi-d), p.183, txt 11022, reads
`[suitably normalized, with respect to j ∈ |F_l|]` with no formula, while Step (x) uses the
average over `j ∈ F_l^⋆`; and Proposition 3.9(iii), p.117, txt 7089, identifies the global
log-volume with an arithmetic degree only `relative to a suitable normalization`.
**What this file does say about them.** Only the *shape* of (M-i), and only on `ℚ_[3]`: if the
reading is a logarithm on the principal units, then "the reading of the `M`-th power is `M` times
the reading of the object" is a theorem (`localLog_pow_eq_smul`), so no separately postulated
divide-back map is needed in that case — division by the scalar `M` does it (`divide_back`). The
toy also exhibits a reading for which exactly this fails
(`naive_magnitude_divide_back_fails`), so the property is not automatic for an arbitrary reading and
"divide by `M`" is not a content-free step.
**What this file does not say.** It does **not** pin the source's `M` (M-ii); it does **not**
construct the divide-back map for the tensor-power Frobenioids of (Ob4-1)/(Ob4-2)/(Ob4-3), and it
proves nothing about the tensor-power twist; it says **nothing** about either normalization of
(M-iii); and it touches none of the log-volume, log-shells, prime-strips, Θ-links, `Ism`, Hodge
theaters, Corollary 3.12, or any object of the audited `external/iut` interfaces. `ℚ_[3]` is a
complete discretely valued field, not the localisation of an arithmetic vector bundle, and
`x ↦ x ^ M` is not `det^{⊗M}`. Nothing here is evidence for or against any IUT claim.
**The `p`-adic mathematics is quoted, not re-proved.** `localLog_pow_eq_smul` is
`PadicLogVolume.padicLog_pow` (`candidates/core-log/PadicLogVolume/PadicLog.lean`) read through the
definition-level identification of the two literal series. One point deserves to be explicit: the
hypothesis `‖x - 1‖ < 1` must hold of *both* `x` and `x ^ M`, otherwise neither side of the law is a
convergent series; that it is preserved under powers is `PadicLogVolume.norm_pow_sub_one_lt`,
re-exported below as `norm_pow_sub_one_lt_Q3`. Convergence itself is not re-proved either; it is
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum`.
**Why `algorithmRun` and `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` are repeated here.**
`candidates/core-transport/lakefile.lean` declares a single library, `lean_lib CoreTransport`, whose
modules are the ones under `CoreTransport/`. `ExecutionProvenance.lean` is a top-level module of the
package, so it is not a Lake target: `lake build ExecutionProvenance` fails with
``unknown target `ExecutionProvenance` `` and no `ExecutionProvenance.olean` exists in
`.lake/build/lib/lean`, so it cannot be imported. The declarations are therefore restated with the
same statements rather than imported; they carry no new mathematics.
namespace DivideBackLaw
noncomputable section
/-! ## 1. The toy algorithm and the two literal series -/
/-- **The finite algorithm**, with the same statement as `ExecutionProvenance.algorithmRun`: the
`n`-th partial sum of the logarithm series at `x`, with term `(-1)^k (x-1)^(k+1)/(k+1)`. This is the
partial-sum algorithm of the `p`-adic logarithm on `ℚ_[3]`, not the η-algorithm of IUT. It is a
plain definition, so it is tied to `localLog` by `algorithmRun_eq_partialSums` (`rfl`) rather than by
an assumption. -/
def algorithmRun (x : ℚ_[3]) (n : ℕ) : ℚ_[3] :=
/-- The algorithm's `n`-th partial sum *is* the `n`-th partial sum of the quoted series term,
definitionally (`rfl`). This is what keeps `algorithmRun` from being decorative: it is the same
sequence whose sum `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` identifies with `CoreTransport.localLog`. -/
theorem algorithmRun_eq_partialSums (x : ℚ_[3]) :
algorithmRun x = fun n : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, PadicLogVolume.logTerm x k := by
funext n
rfl
/-- **Definition-level identification of the two literal series.** `CoreTransport.localLog` and
`PadicLogVolume.padicLog` are the same series, written twice; unfolding both definitions proves it,
so the step carries no mathematical content of its own. It is repeated here — with its companion
`hasSum_logTerm_localLog` — only because `ExecutionProvenance.lean` is not a Lake target and has no
olean (see the module docstring), so it cannot be imported. -/
theorem localLog_eq_padicLog (x : ℚ_[3]) :
CoreTransport.localLog x = PadicLogVolume.padicLog x := by
unfold CoreTransport.localLog PadicLogVolume.padicLog PadicLogVolume.logTerm
rfl
/-- **The existing convergence result, quoted.** For `‖x - 1‖ < 1` the series sums to
`CoreTransport.localLog x`; the proof goes through `CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable`, hence
through the genuine `p`-adic convergence argument and not through `tsum`'s totalised default. -/
theorem hasSum_logTerm_localLog {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
HasSum (PadicLogVolume.logTerm x) (CoreTransport.localLog x) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog x]
exact CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum hx
/-! ## 2. The `M`-th power law, and dividing back by `M` -/
/-- **The domain condition survives powers.** `‖x - 1‖ < 1` implies `‖x ^ M - 1‖ < 1` for every `M`,
so the reading is defined at `x ^ M` as well as at `x`: both sides of the power law below are sums of
a genuinely convergent series. This is `PadicLogVolume.norm_pow_sub_one_lt`, re-exported so that the
preservation is a named fact of this file and not a hidden side condition of the law. -/
theorem norm_pow_sub_one_lt_Q3 (x : ℚ_[3]) (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) (M : ℕ) :
PadicLogVolume.norm_pow_sub_one_lt hx M
/-- **Dividing back by `M`.** The reading of `x` is recovered from the reading of its `M`-th power by
dividing by the scalar `M` — the toy stand-in for "divide back the `M`-th tensor power". The
hypothesis `M ≠ 0` is exactly what the division needs, via `Nat.cast_ne_zero`.
This is the primitive step of the file, and it is placed first for that reason: it is the step the
source omits (M-i), and the multiplied form below is recovered *from* it by multiplying by the same
nonzero scalar, not the other way round.
Note what this does *not* say: it is not a map between two Frobenioids, and the scalar `M` here is a
number, not the `M` of (Ob3-2). -/
theorem divide_back (x : ℚ_[3]) (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) (M : ℕ) (hM0 : M ≠ 0) :
CoreTransport.localLog x = CoreTransport.localLog (x ^ M) / (M : ℚ_[3]) := by
have h := PadicLogVolume.padicLog_pow (p := 3) (k := ℚ_[3]) (by decide)
CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one hx M
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog (x ^ M), localLog_eq_padicLog x, h,
eq_div_iff (Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 hM0)]
ring
/-- **The toy law: the reading of the `M`-th power is `M` times the reading.**
Derived from `divide_back` — which is itself `PadicLogVolume.padicLog_pow`, not re-proved, read
through `localLog_eq_padicLog` at `x ^ M` and at `x`. The domain condition is the one preserved by
`norm_pow_sub_one_lt_Q3`.
The hypothesis `hM : M ≠ 0` is used twice here, and it is not removable from the *route*: both
multiplying the divided law back up and cancelling the scalar require `M` to be invertible in
`ℚ_[3]`. The identity itself does hold at `M = 0` (both sides are then `0`, since `x ^ 0 = 1` and
`localLog 1 = 0`), which is why the hypothesis is carried by the interface rather than by the
mathematics. -/
theorem localLog_pow_eq_smul (x : ℚ_[3]) (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) (M : ℕ) (hM : M ≠ 0) :
CoreTransport.localLog (x ^ M) = (M : ℚ_[3]) * CoreTransport.localLog x := by
have hM' : (M : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 hM
calc CoreTransport.localLog (x ^ M)
= (CoreTransport.localLog (x ^ M) / (M : ℚ_[3])) * (M : ℚ_[3]) := by
rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, eq_div_iff hM']
_ = CoreTransport.localLog x * (M : ℚ_[3]) := by rw [← divide_back x hx M hM]
_ = (M : ℚ_[3]) * CoreTransport.localLog x := mul_comm _ _
/-! ## 3. Anti-degeneracy: the naive magnitude reading has no divide-back
The reading `‖·‖` is the natural competitor to the logarithm: it is also defined on all of
`ℚ_[3]`, it is also a "size". It fails the law, and the failure is concrete — not a negated
universal, and not a statement about a totalised value of a divergent series. -/
/-- **The naive magnitude reading**: the `p`-adic norm of the object. -/
def naiveMagnitude (x : ℚ_[3]) : ℝ := ‖x‖
/-- **Divide back by `M` on the naive magnitude reading**: the magnitude of the `M`-th power, divided
by `M`. This is the operation the logarithm version of the law would suggest for any reading. -/
def naiveDivideBack (x : ℚ_[3]) (M : ℕ) : ℝ := ‖x ^ M‖ / (M : ℝ)
/-- `‖2‖ = 1` in `ℚ_[3]` — the ingredient that makes `4 = 2 ^ 2` a unit rather than a multiple of
`3`. Quoted from `PadicLogVolume.norm_two_eq_one` at `p = 3`. -/
theorem norm_two_Q3 : ‖(2 : ℚ_[3])‖ = 1 :=
PadicLogVolume.norm_two_eq_one (p := 3) (k := ℚ_[3]) (by decide) CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
(by decide)
theorem norm_four_Q3 : ‖(4 : ℚ_[3])‖ = 1 := by
have h : (4 : ℚ_[3]) = 2 ^ 2 := by norm_num
rw [h, norm_pow, norm_two_Q3, one_pow]
/-- `‖4 ^ 2‖ = 1`: `4 ^ 2 = 2 ^ 4` and `‖2‖ = 1`. The `M`-th power of a unit is a unit, which is
precisely why the naive reading has nothing to divide. -/
theorem norm_four_sq_Q3 : ‖((4 : ℚ_[3]) ^ 2)‖ = 1 := by
have h : ((4 : ℚ_[3]) ^ 2) = 2 ^ 4 := by norm_num
rw [h, norm_pow, norm_two_Q3, one_pow]
/-- `4` is a principal unit of `ℚ_[3]`: `‖4 - 1‖ = ‖3‖ = 1/3 < 1`. This is what lets the *logarithm*
reading be applied at `x = 4`, so that the two readings are compared at the same input. -/
theorem norm_four_sub_one_Q3 : ‖(4 : ℚ_[3]) - 1‖ < 1 := by
have h : (4 : ℚ_[3]) - 1 = 3 := by norm_num
rw [h]
exact CoreLog.norm_three_lt_one
/-- **The naive magnitude reading does not divide back.** A concrete failure at `x = 4`, `M = 2`:
`‖4 ^ 2‖ / 2 = 1 / 2`, but `‖4‖ = 1`. The two numbers are separated by `1 / 2 ≠ 1`, so no appeal to
any limiting or totalised quantity is involved: `4` is a unit, its square is a unit, and dividing a
unit's magnitude by `2` leaves `1 / 2`.
This is the anti-degeneracy statement of the file. The same `x` and the same `M` satisfy the
logarithm law (`divide_back_four_two`), so the difference between the two readings is not an artefact
of the input: it is the readings themselves. -/
theorem naive_magnitude_divide_back_fails :
rw [norm_four_sq_Q3, norm_four_Q3]
norm_num
/-- The same failure, stated with the named naive reading: `naiveDivideBack 4 2 ≠ naiveMagnitude 4`.
This is `naive_magnitude_divide_back_fails` after unfolding the two definitions and matching the cast
`((2 : ℕ) : ℝ)` of the definition with the literal `(2 : ℝ)` of the statement. -/
theorem naiveDivideBack_four_two : naiveDivideBack 4 2 ≠ naiveMagnitude 4 := by
have hcast : ((2 : ℕ) : ℝ) = 2 := by norm_num
simpa only [naiveDivideBack, naiveMagnitude, hcast] using naive_magnitude_divide_back_fails
/-- **Non-vacuity of the toy law at the same point.** At `x = 4` and `M = 2` — the very input at
which the naive reading fails — the logarithm version holds: `localLog 4 = localLog (4 ^ 2) / 2`.
Both sides are sums of a convergent series by `norm_four_sub_one_Q3` and `norm_pow_sub_one_lt_Q3`. -/
theorem divide_back_four_two :
CoreTransport.localLog (4 : ℚ_[3]) =
CoreTransport.localLog ((4 : ℚ_[3]) ^ 2) / (2 : ℚ_[3]) :=
divide_back 4 norm_four_sub_one_Q3 2 (by norm_num)
end
end DivideBackLaw
#print axioms DivideBackLaw.algorithmRun
#print axioms DivideBackLaw.algorithmRun_eq_partialSums

#print axioms DivideBackLaw.norm_pow_sub_one_lt_Q3

#print axioms DivideBackLaw.divide_back

# W2 upgrade: compatible transitions on a chain of presentations, and the reading they force
**This file is a toy province, and nothing more.** W2 (`candidates/core-transport/CollectionProvenance.lean`)
put execution provenance on a *collection*, but wired the global reading to the local ones by a single
equation, `globalValue = localValue v`. That equation is a **toy equality**: it is the crudest relation of
the required shape, and it says that a collection's pieces agree *because they are literally the same
value*. Actual local-global data does not have that shape: its pieces are related by **transitions** —
isomorphisms between genuinely different presentations of one object — and a reading attached to those
pieces is well defined only when the transitions are **compatible** (a cocycle/composition law). This
file replaces the toy equality by compatible transitions and proves that a compatible chain forces a
single reading, while an incompatible one does not.
**Why the obligation is exactly this.** `research/core-backward-2026-10-23/h1-decision.md`, §结论一′,
quotes the source (txt lines 8869–8873) defining `n,◦HT^{D-Θ±ellNF}` as the Hodge theater "determined,
**up to isomorphism**, by the various `n,m`-theaters". An object determined only up to isomorphism has no
canonical presentation: a reading built from a *chosen* presentation is a reading of the presentation and
not of the object, unless it is proved independent of that choice. §结论一′ also records that the relevant
indeterminacy is an **orbit** (full poly-isomorphism, h1-coricity.md), so the invariance to be modelled is
invariance across a family of presentations connected by isomorphisms — which is what the transition data
below are. Nothing here asserts that this obligation is discharged for the real object; it exhibits the
shape and proves it on one concrete case.
**The model, on `ℚ_[3]`.** One object, `k ≥ 1` presentations of it, indexed by `Fin k`:
* `input i` — the presentation at index `i`, a principal unit `‖input i - 1‖ < 1` of `ℚ_[3]`;
* `step i j h` — the **transition** from presentation `i` to presentation `j` (`i ≤ j`), a *function*
`ℚ_[3] → ℚ_[3]`, namely multiplication by the principal unit `unit i j h`. Transitions are thus
isomorphisms of the multiplicative structure of the principal units, with inverse `stepInv`; this is
not an equality of inputs (`step_eq`, `stepInv_step`);
* `step_input` — the **elementary** transitions really carry the presentation forward:
`step i (i+1) (input i) = input (i+1)`. This is what makes the `input i` presentations *of one object*;
* `IsCompatible c` — the **cocycle law**: for `i ≤ j ≤ l`, `unit i l = unit i j * unit j l`, i.e. the
transition recorded for the pair `(i,l)` equals the two steps composed. It is a *hypothesis* of the main
theorem, not a field of the structure: an arbitrary chain of presentations-with-transitions need not
satisfy it, and `chainBroken` below does not.
**The reading.** The reading at presentation `i` is `localLog` of the presentation's input transported
**back to the base frame** by the inverse transition from the base to `i`
(`relativeInput i = stepInv (base) i (input i)`). It is computed from the actual data at `i` — the input
there and the transition recorded there — and it is a genuine limit, not a fiat value: `reading_hasSum`
and `reading_is_limit_of_algorithm` show it is the sum, and the limit of the partial sums
`algorithmRun`, of a series that converges at that argument (`relativeInput_mem`). Note that it is *not*
defined as `localLog` of a fixed point; that it nevertheless equals a fixed value on a compatible chain is
the theorem `reading_eq_base`, not the definition.
**What is proved.**
* `input_transport` — on a compatible chain the elementary transports accumulate to the recorded
comparison transition: `input i = input (base) * unit (base) i`. This is the induction where the
cocycle law is used, one step at a time.
* `reading_eq_base`, `reading_compatible` — on a compatible chain every reading equals the base reading,
hence all readings agree. This is the upgrade of W2's toy equality: agreement is now a *consequence* of
the transition data, not an equation imposed on the values.
* `chainCompat` — a compatible chain with explicit numbers (`4, 16, 64 = 4^1, 4^2, 4^3`, units `4^{j-i}`),
whose readings are all `localLog 4` (`chainCompat_reading`).
* `chainBroken` — the same inputs and the same elementary units, but the recorded direct transition
`0 → 2` is `4^3 = 64` instead of `4^2 = 16`. It is **not** compatible
(`chainBroken_not_compatible`) and its readings differ: `localLog 4` at `0` against `localLog 1 = 0` at
`2` (`chainBroken_readings_differ`). This is the anti-degeneracy statement, with explicit numbers and a
concrete witness chain, not a negated universal.
* `difference_lies_in_the_direct_transition` — the two chains have the *same* presentations and the *same*
elementary transitions; only the recorded comparison transition `0 → 2` differs. So the disagreement of
the readings is produced by the transition data alone, which is precisely the feature the toy equality
of W2 had no room for.
**A design point, stated because it is the whole content of item 4.** On the principal units of `ℚ_[3]`
multiplication is *sharply* transitive, and the logarithm is injective there. Hence if the model required
**every** transition to transport the presentation (`step i j (input i) = input j` for all `i ≤ j`), the
comparison units would be determined by the inputs (`unit i j = input j / input i`), the cocycle law would
hold automatically, and every reading would be equal *by construction* — the anti-degeneracy statement
would then be impossible, not merely hard, and no theorem would be left to prove. The model therefore
keeps two sorts of transition data, as the source's localisation data does: the elementary transports that
tie consecutive presentations together (a field, `step_input`), and the comparison transitions from the
base to each presentation (recorded data, `unit (base) i`), whose agreement with the elementary ones is
exactly the cocycle hypothesis. The reading consumes the comparison transition; compatibility is what
makes it independent of the presentation. Nothing here is hidden: `IsCompatible` is stated in full and the
witness of its failure is concrete.
**What this file does not establish.** It says nothing about IUT's localisation data: not about `⊼fQ₁`,
`⊼fQ₂`, the formal quotient `⊼fQ₂ modulo ⊼fQ₁` of §结论二, log-volumes, log-shells, Θ-links, `Ism`,
Corollary 3.12, Hodge theaters, coricity, poly-isomorphisms, Galois actions, prime-strips or Frobenioids.
`Fin k` is a set of indices, not the set of places of a number field; the transitions here are
multiplication by powers of `4` on `ℚ_[3]`, not localisation morphisms; and the logarithm series on
`ℚ_[3]` is not the η-algorithm. In particular the file does **not** show that any reading of the real
object is presentation-independent, and it is not evidence for or against any IUT claim. What it shows is
that the obligation of §结论一′ has a formally checkable shape — reading invariant under a compatible
family of transitions, not under an equality of values — and that in that shape the invariance has a real
hypothesis: drop it and the readings separate, with explicit numbers.
**Why the pieces are restated rather than imported.** `CollectionProvenance.lean`,
`ExecutionProvenance.lean` and `ReadingInvariance.lean` are top-level modules of the package: `lakefile.lean`
declares a single library, `lean_lib CoreTransport`, whose modules are those under `CoreTransport/`, so
those three files are not Lake targets, no `olean` of them exists, and `import CollectionProvenance` is not
available. `algorithmRun`, `localLog_eq_padicLog` and `hasSum_logTerm_localLog` are therefore restated with
the same statements, exactly as the W-files before this one each did, so that this file depends on
`CoreTransport.Basic` and `CoreLog.QpThree` alone. They carry no new mathematics: the first is the
p-adic logarithm's partial-sum algorithm (not the η-algorithm of IUT), the second identifies two literal
series by unfolding both definitions, and the third is `CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum` quoted.
`localLog_four_ne_zero` is likewise restated from W2, together with the remainder estimates it needs
(`norm_logRem_three_le`), since it is the only separation of two readings used below.
Series conventions: the term is the one already used by `CoreTransport.localLog` and by
`PadicLogVolume.logTerm`; convergence on principal units is the existing
`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_hasSum`, quoted rather than re-proved. The `ℚ_[3]` norm facts
(`norm_pow_sub_one_lt`, `norm_inv_sub_one_lt`, `mul_inv_cancel₀`) are used as they stand.
A dependency-footprint block at the end of the file records, for every declaration below, that the only
dependencies are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
