import CoreTransport.Basic
import CoreLog.QpThree
# W10: the H3 synthesis of (M-i) and (M-ii) — one homomorphic reading, one non-torsion probe
**This file is the synthesis of the two toys `DivideBackTwist.lean` (W8, item M-i) and
`ExponentUniqueness.lean` (W9, item M-ii), and nothing more.** Both toys compute on `ℚ_[3]` with the
reading `CoreTransport.localLog`, and both of their conclusions rest on exactly two facts and on
nothing else:
* **additivity** — the reading of a product is the sum of the readings
(`PadicLogVolume.padicLog_mul`, read through `localLog_eq_padicLog`, in the toys);
* **non-torsion of the probe** — the probe's own reading is not zero (`norm_localLog_four`,
`log4_ne_zero` for the probe `4` in the toys).
Nothing further is used in either toy: no root of unity is excluded, no logarithm is inverted, and no
single convergence estimate of the `p`-adic series enters (the estimates in the toys only serve to
*obtain* `localLog 4 ≠ 0`). This file asks what those two facts give **by themselves**, in a setting
where the reading is a homomorphism from a group to the additive group of `ℚ_[3]` and the `p`-adic
analysis is entirely absent.
## Scope: what is proved here
Abstract results (an arbitrary commutative group `G` and an arbitrary reading `R`):
* `reading_pow` — `reading R (x ^ M) = M • reading R x`: the reading is `ℕ`-linear in the exponent.
Both toys' power laws (`localLog_pow_eq_smul`, hence `reading_pow_four`) are this statement with the
`p`-adic logarithm in place of `reading R`.
* `exponent_unique` — at a probe whose reading is non-zero, equal readings of the `M`-th and the
`N`-th powers force `M = N`. This is (M-ii) abstractly: **the exponent is determined exactly when
the probe has non-zero reading**. W9's `power_reading_injective_on_probe` is the case
`x = 4`, `reading = localLog`.
* `twist_free_iff` — the twist `u` contributes nothing to any reading, i.e. `∀ x, reading R (u * x) =
reading R x`, exactly when `reading R u = 0`. This is (M-i)'s condition "the twist term vanishes"
turned into an `iff`; W8's `twist_insensitive_iff` is the analogous statement with the twist
residue `localLog u` in place of `reading R u`.
* `divideBack_abstract` — dividing the reading of the twisted `M`-th power by the scalar `M` leaves
the twist's own reading visible: `reading R (u * x ^ M) / M = reading R u / M + reading R x`. This
is W8's `divideBack_twist` with `localLog` replaced by an arbitrary additive reading, and with the
residue `localLog u` replaced by `reading R u`.
* `comparison_well_defined` — **the divide-back conclusion** of (M-i): twist-free (`reading R u = 0`)
is enough to get the probe's reading back from the divide-back of the twisted `M`-th power. The
probe condition `reading R x ≠ 0` is **not** an hypothesis of this statement — it belongs to
`exponent_unique`, which is the (M-ii) half. (An earlier version carried it unused and silenced the
linter; the hypothesis was dropped instead.)
Degeneracy, in both directions. To keep the numbers literal and the file free of `p`-adic analysis,
the witnesses live in the free commutative group `Multiplicative ℤ` on one generator (its
multiplication is the addition of `ℤ`, so `ofAdd 1` is a genuine non-identity element and `ofAdd n`
is "the twist whose reading is `n`"):
* `exponent_unique_fails_at_zero_reading` — at a probe that is *not* the identity but whose reading is
zero, two different exponents give the same reading. The hypothesis of `exponent_unique` is
load-bearing, and the failure is not an artefact of the unit `1`: `zero_reading_powers_agree` gives
the abstract version, for an arbitrary zero-reading probe.
* `comparison_fails_at_four` — at the twist `4`, the probe `1` and `M = 2` — the same numbers as
W8's `divideBack_twist_four_one` — the hypothesis `reading R u = 0` is false (`reading_twistFour_ne_zero`)
and the conclusion of `comparison_well_defined` is **false**: the divide-back reads `4 / 2 = 2`,
while the probe's reading is `0`.
## The encoding of the reading, and why it is this one
The intended object is a homomorphism from the multiplicative group `G` to the *additive* group of
`ℚ_[3]`, i.e. a map with `R (x * y) = R x + R y`. An `AddMonoidHom` cannot be used directly: the type
`G →+ H` demands an `AddMonoid` structure on `G`, while `G` here carries only a `CommGroup`. The
reading is therefore encoded as a **monoid** homomorphism `R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]`, whose
multiplication *is* the addition of `ℚ_[3]`, and `reading R` is its additive shadow,
`reading R x = (R x).toAdd`. This is not a weakening: by Mathlib's `MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft`, such an
`R` is literally the same thing as an additive monoid homomorphism `Additive G →+ ℚ_[3]`
(`reading_eq_toAdditiveLeft`), and the additivity used everywhere below,
`reading R (x * y) = reading R x + reading R y` (`reading_mul`), is `Multiplicative.toAdd_mul`
transported along `map_mul`. Nothing else about the encoding is used, and no statement below mentions
`Multiplicative` except this shadow. (`CommGroup` is kept, as in the task and as in the toys' groups,
although no proof below uses commutativity: `map_mul`, `pow_succ` and `mul_one` suffice.)
## What this file does not say
It does **not** say that any object of the theory carries such a reading. `ℚ_[3]` is the `p`-adic
field, not a log-volume; `x ↦ x ^ M` is not `det^{⊗M}`; `reading R` is neither `localLog` nor a
log-volume of any arithmetic line bundle. No tensor-power Frobenius, log-shell, prime-strip,
Θ-link, Hodge theater, `Ism`, or Corollary 3.12 appears, and no audited `external/iut` interface is
touched. In particular the degeneracy witnesses do **not** exhibit a zero-reading probe "in the
source's fiber", and the twist `4` of `comparison_fails_at_four` is an element of the free group whose
reading is the integer `4`, not W8's `4 ∈ ℚ_[3]` whose reading is `localLog 4` (W8 proves
`‖localLog 4‖ = 1/3`; that estimate is *not* redone here, and it is not the point of the witness). The
load-bearing hypothesis in that witness is `reading R u ≠ 0`, which holds in the toys for `u = 4` and
holds here for the integer `4` alike. Nothing here is evidence for or against any claim of the
source.
The abstraction is honest in the following precise sense: it isolates the two facts the two toys
actually use — additivity of the reading, and non-vanishing of the probe's reading — and derives from
them exactly what those two facts imply. It therefore says **what W8 and W9 share**, and it does not
say that anything in IUT supplies such an `R`, nor that the source's assertions about tensor-power
twists and the exponent `M` are true: those remain open, as recorded in
`research/core-backward-2026-10-23/m-i-design.md` and `m-ii-design.md`.
namespace H3Synthesis
noncomputable section
variable {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
/-! ## 1. The reading: a group homomorphism written additively -/
/-- **The additive shadow of a reading.** For `R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]` — a homomorphism from
the multiplicative group `G` into the multiplicative copy of the *additive* group `ℚ_[3]` — the
reading of `x` is the element of `ℚ_[3]` it names: `reading R x = (R x).toAdd`. By
`reading_eq_toAdditiveLeft` this is the same function as `MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft R` on
`Additive.ofMul x`, so it is an additive monoid homomorphism `Additive G →+ ℚ_[3]` in disguise. -/
def reading (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (x : G) : ℚ_[3] :=
Multiplicative.toAdd (R x)
/-- **`reading R` is the additive homomorphism attached to `R`.** Mathlib's
`MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft` turns a monoid homomorphism `G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]` into an additive
monoid homomorphism `Additive G →+ ℚ_[3]`; this theorem records that `reading R` is that
homomorphism, composed with `Additive.ofMul`. It is the reason the encoding `G →* Multiplicative
ℚ_[3]` loses nothing with respect to the intended `G →+ ℚ_[3]`. -/
theorem reading_eq_toAdditiveLeft (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (x : G) :
reading R x = MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft R (Additive.ofMul x) := rfl
/-- **Additivity of the reading.** The reading of a product is the sum of the readings; this is the
one property of the two toys' `localLog` that their computations actually use
(`PadicLogVolume.padicLog_mul` for W8/W9). -/
theorem reading_mul (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (x y : G) :
reading R (x * y) = reading R x + reading R y := by
simp [reading]
/-- **The reading of the identity is zero**, so a unit reading nothing may serve as the "no twist"
element of `twist_free_iff`. -/
theorem reading_one (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) : reading R (1 : G) = 0 := by
simp [reading]
/-! ## 2. The reading is `ℕ`-linear in the exponent, and pins the exponent when non-zero -/
/-- **The reading of the `M`-th power is `M` times the reading.** Proved from additivity
(`reading_mul`) by induction on `M`; no hypothesis on `M` is needed, and the case `M = 0` holds
because the reading of the identity is zero. This is the abstract form of the toys' power law
`localLog_pow_eq_smul`, hence of W9's `reading_pow_four`. -/
theorem reading_pow (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (x : G) (M : ℕ) :
reading R (x ^ M) = M • reading R x := by
induction M with
| zero => simp [reading_one]
| succ M ih => rw [pow_succ, reading_mul, ih, succ_nsmul]
/-- **(M-ii) abstractly: a probe with non-zero reading determines the exponent.** If the probe `x` has
`reading R x ≠ 0`, then two powers of `x` have the same reading exactly when the exponents agree.
* Forward: `reading_pow` turns the hypothesis into `M • reading R x = N • reading R x`, i.e.
`(M : ℚ_[3]) * reading R x = (N : ℚ_[3]) * reading R x`; the non-zero element `reading R x` is
cancellable in the field `ℚ_[3]` (`mul_right_cancel₀`), and `Nat.cast_injective` concludes `M = N`.
* Backward: congruence.
This is W9's `power_reading_injective_on_probe` with the probe `4` and the reading `localLog`
replaced by an arbitrary probe and an arbitrary additive reading. The hypothesis `reading R x ≠ 0` is
exactly the non-torsion condition: it is what makes the cancellation available, and
`exponent_unique_fails_at_zero_reading` shows it cannot be dropped. -/
theorem exponent_unique (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (x : G) (hx : reading R x ≠ 0) {M N : ℕ} :
reading R (x ^ M) = reading R (x ^ N) ↔ M = N := by
rw [reading_pow, reading_pow]
constructor
· intro h
rw [nsmul_eq_mul, nsmul_eq_mul] at h
exact Nat.cast_injective (R := ℚ_[3]) (mul_right_cancel₀ hx h)
· intro h
rw [h]
/-! ## 3. (M-i): the twist term vanishes exactly when the twist reads zero -/
/-- **(M-i)'s vanishing condition, as an `iff`.** A twist `u` contributes nothing to the reading of
any product — `∀ x, reading R (u * x) = reading R x` — exactly when its own reading is zero.
* Forward: additivity and `reading R u = 0` give `0 + reading R x = reading R x`.
* Backward: instantiate the insensitivity at `x = 1`; then `reading R (u * 1) = reading R 1 = 0`, and
`reading R (u * 1) = reading R u`.
This is W8's `twist_insensitive_iff` with `localLog` generalised to an additive reading, and with the
twist's residue `localLog u` generalised to `reading R u`. -/
theorem twist_free_iff (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (u : G) :
reading R u = 0 ↔ ∀ x : G, reading R (u * x) = reading R x := by
constructor
· intro h x
rw [reading_mul, h, zero_add]
· intro h
simpa [reading_one] using h 1
/-- **(M-i) abstractly: the divide-back, with the twist term visible.** Dividing the reading of the
twisted `M`-th power `u * x ^ M` by the scalar `M` gives the twist's own reading divided by `M`, plus
the reading of `x` — the twist term is not removed by the divide-back. The hypothesis `M ≠ 0` is
exactly what the division needs (`Nat.cast_ne_zero`).
This is W8's `divideBack_twist` (`localLog ((u * x) ^ M) / M = localLog u + localLog x`) with the
`p`-adic logarithm replaced by an arbitrary additive reading; the summand `reading R u / M` is the
abstract counterpart of W8's `twistResidue u`. -/
theorem divideBack_abstract (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (u x : G) (M : ℕ) (hM : M ≠ 0) :
reading R (u * x ^ M) / (M : ℚ_[3]) = reading R u / (M : ℚ_[3]) + reading R x := by
have hM' : (M : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr hM
rw [reading_mul, reading_pow, nsmul_eq_mul, add_div, mul_div_cancel_left₀ (reading R x) hM']
/-- **The divide-back conclusion.** If the twist reads zero (`reading R u = 0`, the twist-free condition
of `twist_free_iff`), then the divide-back of the twisted `M`-th power *is* the reading of the probe: the
twist term is absent, so dividing by `M` is harmless.
This is the (M-i) half of the synthesis and it is stated **without** the probe hypothesis, because the
identity does not need it — the previous version carried `reading R x ≠ 0` as an unused hypothesis and
silenced the linter; that is fixed here by dropping the hypothesis instead of the warning. The (M-ii)
half, that the surviving reading determines `M`, is `exponent_unique`, which is where the probe condition
actually belongs. -/
theorem comparison_well_defined (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (u x : G) (hu : reading R u = 0)
reading R (u * x ^ M) / (M : ℚ_[3]) = reading R x := by
rw [divideBack_abstract R u x M hM, hu, zero_div, zero_add]
/-! ## 4. Degeneracy: the two hypotheses are load-bearing
The witnesses below live in the free commutative group `Multiplicative ℤ` on one generator, whose
multiplication is the addition of `ℤ`. This keeps every number literal and keeps the file free of
`p`-adic analysis: the reading of `ofAdd n` is the integer `n`, cast into `ℚ_[3]`. -/
/-- **The trivial reading on the free group**: every element reads `0`. Its kernel is everything, so
no probe whatsoever is non-torsion for it. -/
def trivialReading : Multiplicative ℤ →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3] where
toFun _ := 1
map_one' := rfl
map_mul' := by
intro a b
simp
/-- **The free reading**: the generator `ofAdd 1` reads `1`, so `ofAdd n` reads the integer `n` cast
into `ℚ_[3]`. It is `Int.castAddHom ℚ_[3]` transported to multiplicative notation by Mathlib's
`AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicative`, i.e. an honest additive homomorphism out of `Multiplicative ℤ`. -/
def freeReading : Multiplicative ℤ →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3] :=
(Int.castAddHom ℚ_[3]).toMultiplicative
/-- The probe of the first degeneracy witness: the generator of the free group. -/
def probeOne : Multiplicative ℤ := Multiplicative.ofAdd 1
/-- The twist of the second degeneracy witness: the free-group element named `4`, i.e. the fourth
power of the generator. Its reading is the integer `4`. -/
def twistFour : Multiplicative ℤ := Multiplicative.ofAdd 4
/-- The free reading computes: `ofAdd n` reads `n`. -/
theorem reading_freeReading (n : ℤ) :
reading freeReading (Multiplicative.ofAdd n) = (n : ℚ_[3]) := by
simp [reading, freeReading]
/-- The probe of the first witness is **not** the identity: `ofAdd 1 ≠ ofAdd 0`. This is what makes
the first degeneracy a statement about a non-identity probe with zero reading, rather than about the
unit. -/
theorem probeOne_ne_one : probeOne ≠ 1 := by
intro h
have h' : (1 : ℤ) = 0 := by
simpa [probeOne] using congrArg Multiplicative.toAdd h
exact one_ne_zero h'
/-- The probe of the first witness reads zero under the trivial reading. -/
theorem zeroReading_probeOne : reading trivialReading probeOne = 0 := by
simp [reading, trivialReading, probeOne]
/-- **Abstract degeneracy of (M-ii): a probe with zero reading determines nothing.** If
`reading R x = 0`, then the readings of the `M`-th and the `N`-th powers of `x` agree for *every*
pair of exponents, with no hypothesis relating them. So the non-vanishing hypothesis of
`exponent_unique` is not a convenience: on the zero-reading part of `G` the conclusion fails for all
theorem zero_reading_powers_agree (R : G →* Multiplicative ℚ_[3]) (x : G) (hx : reading R x = 0)
(M N : ℕ) : reading R (x ^ M) = reading R (x ^ N) := by
simp [reading_pow, hx]
/-- **Degeneracy of (M-ii), with numbers: the non-identity probe `ofAdd 1` under the trivial reading
gives the same reading at the exponents `0` and `1`.** The statement bundles the four facts that make
it a genuine counterexample to the conclusion of `exponent_unique` without its hypothesis: the probe
is not the identity, its reading is zero, the readings of the two powers agree, and the exponents
differ. So `exponent_unique` genuinely fails once its hypothesis is dropped. -/
theorem exponent_unique_fails_at_zero_reading :
probeOne ≠ 1 ∧ reading trivialReading probeOne = 0 ∧
reading trivialReading (probeOne ^ 0) = reading trivialReading (probeOne ^ 1) ∧
⟨probeOne_ne_one, zeroReading_probeOne,
zero_reading_powers_agree trivialReading probeOne zeroReading_probeOne 0 1, by norm_num⟩
/-- The twist of the second witness reads `4`. -/
theorem reading_twistFour : reading freeReading twistFour = 4 := by
rw [twistFour, reading_freeReading]
norm_num
/-- **The twist of the second witness has non-zero reading**: `reading R u ≠ 0`, so the hypothesis
`hu` (the twist-free hypothesis) of `comparison_well_defined` is false at these numbers. -/
theorem reading_twistFour_ne_zero : reading freeReading twistFour ≠ 0 := by
rw [reading_twistFour]
exact Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (by norm_num)
/-- **Degeneracy of (M-i), with W8's numbers.** At the twist `4`, the probe `1` and `M = 2` — the
numbers of W8's `divideBack_twist_four_one` — the twist has non-zero reading, and then the conclusion
of `comparison_well_defined` is *false*: the divide-back reads `4 / 2 = 2`, while the probe's reading
is `0`. So the hypothesis `reading R u = 0` is load-bearing, and "divide back by `M`" alone does not
remove the twist term.
The inequality is stated as an inequality of the two readings, as required: the left side is the
divide-back of the twisted second power, the right side is the reading of the probe. -/
theorem comparison_fails_at_four :
reading freeReading (twistFour * (1 : Multiplicative ℤ) ^ 2) / ((2 : ℕ) : ℚ_[3]) ≠
reading freeReading (1 : Multiplicative ℤ) := by
have h2 : ((2 : ℕ) : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 (by norm_num)
exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ ((2 : ℕ) : ℚ_[3]) h2
rw [divideBack_abstract freeReading twistFour 1 2 (by norm_num), reading_twistFour, reading_one,
add_zero, h42]
exact h2
end
end H3Synthesis

# W11: the (9-1) shape in a toy — two families of maps of pointed lines, and equality on one orbit
**Scope.** This file formalises, in the smallest model in which the statement has any content, the *shape*
of the compatibility question that `research/core-backward-2026-10-23/lana-report-assessment.md` §5b calls
**(9-1)**: two constructions of an isomorphism between the same pair of **pointed lines**, one of them
`η_q` (a single map, fixed by the `q`-pilot) and one of them `η^anab_S` (a family of maps, indexed by a
choice `S`), and the question whether some `S` makes the two equal. It is a toy province: not a fact-tree
entry, not a registry entry, not an audit of any IUT object. The core GAP of
`research/core-backward-2026-10-23/` stays OPEN.
**The obligation, quoted.** The reduction this file models is already in the audited upstream interface.
`reviews/core-round/external/iut/Iut/Wall/EtaAlg.lean:151` states
theorem etaAnab_eq_etaQ_iff {h₁ h₂ : A.Side} (ι : A.Choice (A.qBPS h₂) h₁) (S : Ind3 D) :
A.etaAnab ι S = etaQ D ↔ logVol D (A.out ι S) = (concreteVariantData D).qPilot.lhs
and the docstring of that file says of it: "(9-1) for `(ι, S)` holds iff `log-vol(out ι S) = −|log(q)|`:
an equation between two maps of pointed lines *is* an equation of real numbers". The mechanism is
`ValBPS.eta_eq_eta_iff` (`Iut/Wall/BPS.lean:335`): a linear map of the pointed line is determined by the
image of the pilot, so two such maps agree iff they agree at that one point. Everything in the present file
is the elementary linear algebra behind that sentence, over `ℝ`, with the indeterminacy made explicit.
**What is modelled, and what is not.** `R^val` and `R^ss` are `ℝ` and `ℝ` (both one-dimensional, both
pointed), a map between them is `ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ`, and the pointing is a chosen non-zero real number `p` (the
pilot). The two families are: `etaAnab c s = scalarMap (c s)` for a family of scalars `c : S → ℝ` indexed
by the choice `S`, and `etaQ q = scalarMap q` for a single scalar `q`. The map `scalarMap a` is
multiplication by `a`, which is what `ValBPS.eta` is after the pilot coordinate is put on the source
(`eta x = x • pilotCoord`). The structural cost of the model is that the "same pair of pointed lines" is
the same two copies of `ℝ` — which is exactly the point: (9-1) is not about the spaces, it is about which
isomorphism between them the two constructions produce.
**What is proved, in order.**
1. **The reduction lemma** (`map_eq_iff_pilot`): for `f g : ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ` and `p ≠ 0`,
`f = g ↔ f p = g p`. Forward is congruence; backward is `LinearMap.ext` on the basis vector `p`, using
`x = (x / p) • p` — the single place where `p ≠ 0` is consumed. `map_eq_scalarMap` is the companion
uniqueness statement: every map of the pointed line is `scalarMap` of its value at `1`.
2. **A family of candidate isomorphisms, and (9-1) as a scalar equation** (`etaAnab`, `etaQ`,
`eta_equality_iff_scalar`): `etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q ↔ c S₀ = q`. This is the toy form of
`etaAnab_eq_etaQ_iff`, with `c S₀` in the role of `logVol D (A.out ι S)` and `q` in the role of
`(concreteVariantData D).qPilot.lhs`. The file also states the pilot-level form
(`eta_equality_iff_pilot`, `eta_equality_iff_scalar_via_pilot`), so that the chain
"equality of maps ⟺ agreement at the pilot ⟺ equality of scalars" is proved and not merely asserted.
`etaQ_bijective` and `etaAnab_bijective` record that a member of either family is an isomorphism of
pointed lines exactly when its scalar is non-zero — a *candidate* isomorphism with a zero scalar is a
collapse, which is where §5's second degeneracy lives.
3. **The orbit form** (`InOrbit`, `orbitFamily`, `eta_eq_iff_inOrbit`,
`in_orbit_iff_exists_iso_in_family`): the group `ℝˣ` acts on the scalars by `u • x = u * x`
(`unit_smul_eq_mul`), a subgroup `H ≤ ℝˣ` is the indeterminacy, and `orbitFamily H c₀ s = s • c₀` is the
family indexed **by the indeterminacy itself** — the toy stand-in for "(Ind3)-choice `S`". Then
`(∃ s : H, etaAnab (orbitFamily H c₀) s = etaQ q) ↔ InOrbit H c₀ q`, i.e. *equality of maps, equality of
scalars, and orbit membership are one statement*, and the form with the orbit condition inside the
existential (`in_orbit_iff_exists_iso_in_family`) is proved as well. `exists_S_of_inOrbit` is the
constructive direction: an orbit member *produces* the choice `S`. `nine_one_at_four` records one case
where the toy's (9-1) holds with an explicit witness, and `top_inOrbit_iff` records that with the whole
unit group as indeterminacy the orbit of a non-zero scalar is every non-zero scalar — so in this toy the
obstruction is concentrated exactly at `q = 0`.
4. **Degeneracy with the pilot zero** (`idMap`, `doubleMap`, `agreement_at_zero_not_determining`,
`zero_pilot_not_determining`, `map_eq_iff_pilot_fails_at_zero`): `idMap` (multiplication by `1`) and
`doubleMap` (multiplication by `2`) are different maps with `idMap 0 = 0 = doubleMap 0`. So without
`p ≠ 0` the reduction lemma is false, and the hypothesis of item 1 is not removable.
5. **Degeneracy with the scalar outside the orbit** (two witnesses, both computed, not assumed):
with the trivial indeterminacy `H = ⊥` the family is the single map `scalarMap 1`, the target scalar is
`2`, and `2` is not in the orbit of `1` (`not_inOrbit_bot`): `bottom_pointwise` exhibits the failure at
the pilot (`1` against `2`) and `no_S_below_bottom` proves that no choice gives equality — although
every involved map is an isomorphism, so this is *not* the zero-collapse of item 2 but a genuine failure
of orbit membership. And
with `H = ⊤` and target scalar `0`, `no_S_top_zero` proves that no choice gives equality, because the
whole unit orbit of `1` misses `0` (`top_inOrbit_iff`): this is the case where the target is the zero
map, so its own pilot is zero and it is not an isomorphism at all.
6. **A dependency-footprint line per declaration**, at the end of the file: every declaration, the `def`s
and `abbrev`s included, prints a subset of `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}`.
**Restated, not imported.** The single import is `CoreLog.QpThree`, which supplies the ambient Mathlib
(`ℝ`, `LinearMap`, the unit group of `ℝ` and its subgroups). Nothing else in this repository is imported: the other
files of `candidates/core-transport/` are top-level modules of the package, are not Lake targets, have no
`olean`, and so cannot be imported — but nothing of them is needed here either, since the content of this
file is elementary linear algebra over `ℝ` and is written out in full. The upstream `Iut` files are a
different package with no dependency on this one, so `etaAnab_eq_etaQ_iff` and `eta_eq_eta_iff` are
**quoted** in this docstring and appear nowhere in the code: this file defines its own `etaAnab` and
`etaQ`, which are unrelated Lean constants that happen to share the names of the upstream ones.
**Non-claims.**
1. **It does not prove (9-1).** What is proved is a statement about `ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ`; (9-1) is a statement about
`A.etaAnab ι S` and `etaQ D`, which are linear maps out of a value-group BPS `B.val.C` built from
`out`, `BPS`, `Ind3`, `logVol` and `qPilot`. None of those objects occurs here.
2. **No `out`, no `BPS`, no `Ind3`, no `logVol`, no Θ-link, no Hodge theater, no volume container, no
log-shell, no `Ism`, no `Ind1`/`Ind2`, no `q`-pilot as an arithmetic object** occurs in the code. The
index type `S` of the family is an arbitrary type; `H` is an arbitrary subgroup of `ℝˣ`; `c` is an
arbitrary function `S → ℝ`, not a log-volume; `q` is an arbitrary real, not `−|log q|`.
3. **The toy's (9-1) is a theorem of the toy only.** In the toy, "there is a choice `S` with equality" is
*equivalent* to a scalar being in an orbit, and both directions are proved; that equivalence is a fact
about multiplication on `ℝ` and carries no information about the real constructions. The upstream
`Wall` hypothesis is an *open* proposition about those constructions; this file neither implies nor
refutes it.
4. **The indeterminacy is not modelled as an action on `S`.** `Ind1`/`Ind2` act on the (Ind3)-choices
upstream ([LANA] §10.4); here the family is simply indexed by the subgroup and no action on the index
set is defined, so the file says nothing about how the choices are permuted, only about which scalars
they produce.
5. **No evidence for or against any IUT claim.** The core GAP stays OPEN.
The file is written to the house discipline: no unfinished proof, no extra assumption, no decision
procedure by computation, and the footprint block at the end certifies the three standard principles.

/-! ## 1. Pointed lines, and the reduction lemma -/
/-- **The source pointed line** `R^val` ([LANA] §9.3: the value-group portion, carrying a canonical
pilot), as a toy: the one-dimensional real vector space `ℝ`. The pointing is not a structure here; it is
the non-zero real `p` that the theorems below take as an argument. -/
abbrev Rval : Type := ℝ
/-- **The target pointed line** `R^ss` ([LANA] §9.3: the unit monoid, log, log-shells, volume containers),
as a toy: again `ℝ`. That the two spaces coincide is deliberate — the content of (9-1) is which
isomorphism between them a construction produces, not what the spaces are. -/
abbrev Rss : Type := ℝ
/-- Both pointed lines are one-dimensional, which is the only structural fact the reduction lemma uses:
a single non-zero vector is a basis. -/
theorem finrank_Rval : Module.finrank ℝ Rval = 1 := Module.finrank_self ℝ
/-- The target pointed line is one-dimensional as well. -/
theorem finrank_Rss : Module.finrank ℝ Rss = 1 := Module.finrank_self ℝ
/-- **The map of pointed lines "multiplication by `a`"**: `x ↦ a * x`. Every map of pointed lines is of
this form for exactly one `a` (`map_eq_scalarMap`), so this is the toy shape of `ValBPS.eta`, which sends
the pilot of the source to the real number `a` and extends by linearity. -/
def scalarMap (a : ℝ) : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss := LinearMap.mulLeft ℝ a
/-- The computation rule of `scalarMap`. -/
theorem scalarMap_apply (a x : ℝ) : scalarMap a x = a * x := LinearMap.mulLeft_apply ℝ a x
/-- **The scalar is recovered from the map**: evaluating at `1` inverts `scalarMap`. This is the "pointed"
half of the structure — the value at a non-zero point determines the scalar, hence the map. -/
theorem scalarMap_injective : Function.Injective scalarMap := by
intro a b h
have h1 : scalarMap a 1 = scalarMap b 1 := LinearMap.congr_fun h 1
rwa [scalarMap_apply, scalarMap_apply, mul_one, mul_one] at h1
/-- **The reduction lemma: two maps of pointed lines are equal iff they agree at the pilot.** This is the
elementary content of `ValBPS.eta_eq_eta_iff`, and hence of `etaAnab_eq_etaQ_iff`: the forward direction
is congruence, and the backward direction is `LinearMap.ext` on the basis `1 = (1 / p) • p` — every `x` is
`(x / p) • p`, so the value at `p` propagates to every `x`. The hypothesis `p ≠ 0` is exactly what makes
that a basis, and §4 exhibits two different maps agreeing at `0`. -/
theorem map_eq_iff_pilot (f g : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss) (p : ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
f = g ↔ f p = g p := by
constructor
· intro h
exact LinearMap.congr_fun h p
· intro h
refine LinearMap.ext fun x => ?_
have hx : x = (x / p) • p := by
rw [smul_eq_mul, div_mul_cancel₀ x hp]
calc f x = f ((x / p) • p) := congrArg f hx
_ = (x / p) • f p := LinearMap.map_smul f (x / p) p
_ = (x / p) • g p := by rw [h]
_ = g ((x / p) • p) := (LinearMap.map_smul g (x / p) p).symm
_ = g x := congrArg g hx.symm
/-- **Every map of the pointed line is multiplication by its value at `1`** — the companion uniqueness
statement to `map_eq_iff_pilot`, and the toy form of `ValBPS.eta_unique`: a map of pointed lines has no
freedom beyond the image of one non-zero point. -/
theorem map_eq_scalarMap (f : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss) : f = scalarMap (f 1) := by
refine LinearMap.ext fun x => ?_
rw [scalarMap_apply]
calc f x = f (x • (1 : ℝ)) := congrArg f (by rw [smul_eq_mul, mul_one])
_ = x • f 1 := LinearMap.map_smul f x 1
_ = f 1 * x := by rw [smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
/-! ## 2. A family of candidate isomorphisms, and (9-1) as an equation of numbers -/
/-- **The toy `η^anab`**: the family of maps of pointed lines indexed by the choice `S`, given by the
family of scalars `c : S → ℝ`. Upstream, `A.etaAnab ι S` is `B.val.eta (logVol D (A.out ι S))`; here
`c S₀` plays the role of that log-volume, and `S` is an arbitrary index type. -/
def etaAnab {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (s : S) : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss := scalarMap (c s)
/-- **The toy `η_q`**: the single map fixed by the scalar `q`, which plays the role of the `q`-pilot's
left-hand side `(concreteVariantData D).qPilot.lhs`. -/
def etaQ (q : ℝ) : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss := scalarMap q
/-- The computation rule of the family at a point of the source. -/
theorem etaAnab_apply {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (s : S) (x : ℝ) : etaAnab c s x = c s * x := by
rw [etaAnab, scalarMap_apply]
/-- The computation rule of `etaQ` at a point of the source. -/
theorem etaQ_apply (q x : ℝ) : etaQ q x = q * x := by
rw [etaQ, scalarMap_apply]
/-- **A member of the family is an isomorphism of pointed lines iff its scalar is non-zero** — the reason
the family is called a family of *candidate* isomorphisms: a zero scalar collapses the pointed line. -/
theorem etaAnab_bijective {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (s : S) (hc : c s ≠ 0) :
Function.Bijective (etaAnab c s) := by
have h : (etaAnab c s : Rval → Rss) = fun x => c s * x := by
funext x
rw [etaAnab_apply]
rw [h]
exact mulLeft_bijective₀ (c s) hc
/-- **`etaQ q` is an isomorphism of pointed lines iff `q ≠ 0`** — the same statement for the single map. -/
theorem etaQ_bijective {q : ℝ} (hq : q ≠ 0) : Function.Bijective (etaQ q) := by
have h : (etaQ q : Rval → Rss) = fun x => q * x := by
funext x
rw [etaQ_apply]
rw [h]
exact mulLeft_bijective₀ q hq
/-- **The scalar equation is solvable in the pilot**: `c * p = q * p ↔ c = q` for `p ≠ 0`. This is the
step that turns "the two maps have the same value at the pilot" into an equation of numbers. -/
theorem pilot_eq_iff_scalar (c q p : ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) : c * p = q * p ↔ c = q := by
constructor
· intro h
exact mul_right_cancel₀ hp h
· rintro rfl
rfl
/-- **The pilot-level form of the reduction**: `etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q` iff the two maps agree at the
pilot `p`. This is `map_eq_iff_pilot` at the two families, and it is the first link of the chain. -/
theorem eta_equality_iff_pilot {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (q p : ℝ) (S₀ : S) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q ↔ etaAnab c S₀ p = etaQ q p :=
map_eq_iff_pilot _ _ p hp
/-- **The full chain at the pilot**: equality of maps ⟺ agreement at the pilot ⟺ equality of the two
scalars. The middle step is `pilot_eq_iff_scalar`, i.e. cancellation of the non-zero pilot. -/
theorem eta_equality_iff_scalar_via_pilot {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (q p : ℝ) (S₀ : S) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q ↔ c S₀ = q := by
rw [eta_equality_iff_pilot c q p S₀ hp, etaAnab, etaQ, scalarMap_apply, scalarMap_apply,
pilot_eq_iff_scalar (c S₀) q p hp]
/-- **(9-1) for one choice `S₀` is an equation of real numbers**: `etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q ↔ c S₀ = q`.
This is the toy counterpart of `etaAnab_eq_etaQ_iff`, which says the same thing with `c S₀` replaced by
`logVol D (A.out ι S)` and `q` by `(concreteVariantData D).qPilot.lhs`: here the equation is decided at
the pilot `1`, so the statement is the `p = 1` case of `eta_equality_iff_scalar_via_pilot` and needs no
hypothesis. -/
theorem eta_equality_iff_scalar {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (q : ℝ) (S₀ : S) :
etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q ↔ c S₀ = q :=
eta_equality_iff_scalar_via_pilot c q 1 S₀ one_ne_zero
/-- **Existence of a choice, as an equation of numbers**: some `S₀` gives equality of maps iff some `S₀`
has its scalar equal to `q`. This is the quantifier form that (9-1) actually asks for. -/
theorem exists_eta_eq_iff_exists_scalar {S : Type*} (c : S → ℝ) (q : ℝ) :
(∃ S₀ : S, etaAnab c S₀ = etaQ q) ↔ ∃ S₀ : S, c S₀ = q := by
constructor
· rintro ⟨S₀, h⟩
exact ⟨S₀, (eta_equality_iff_scalar c q S₀).mp h⟩
· rintro ⟨S₀, h⟩
exact ⟨S₀, (eta_equality_iff_scalar c q S₀).mpr h⟩
/-! ## 3. The orbit form
The group `ℝˣ` of units acts on the scalars by multiplication, `u • x = u * x`. A subgroup `H ≤ ℝˣ` is
the indeterminacy, and the family of candidate isomorphisms is indexed **by the indeterminacy itself**:
the choice `S` of (9-1) is, in this toy, the choice of an element of `H`, and the scalar it produces is
`s • c₀`. That is what makes the orbit statement an *equivalence* rather than an analogy. -/
/-- The action of the units of `ℝ` on the scalars: `u • x = u * x`. -/
theorem unit_smul_eq_mul (u : ℝˣ) (x : ℝ) : u • x = (u : ℝ) * x := by
rw [Units.smul_def, smul_eq_mul]
/-- **The orbit of a scalar under the indeterminacy**: `q` is obtained from `c` by some `u ∈ H`, i.e.
`q = u * c`. This is the toy form of "[LANA] §9.3: `η_q` lies in the orbit of the `η^anab_S`" — the
"analogue of a Teichmüller deformation" of the report. -/
def InOrbit (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c q : ℝ) : Prop := ∃ u : ℝˣ, u ∈ H ∧ q = (u : ℝ) * c
/-- The orbit condition written with the group action: `q = u • c`. -/
theorem inOrbit_iff_exists_smul (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c q : ℝ) :
InOrbit H c q ↔ ∃ u : ℝˣ, u ∈ H ∧ q = u • c := by
simp only [InOrbit, unit_smul_eq_mul]
/-- The orbit condition with the witness living in the subgroup rather than in `ℝˣ`. -/
theorem inOrbit_iff_exists_unit (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c q : ℝ) :
InOrbit H c q ↔ ∃ u : H, q = ((u : ℝˣ) : ℝ) * c := by
constructor
· rintro ⟨u, hu, hq⟩
exact ⟨⟨u, hu⟩, hq⟩
· rintro ⟨u, hq⟩
exact ⟨(u : ℝˣ), u.2, hq⟩
/-- **The family of candidate isomorphisms, indexed by the indeterminacy**: at `s : H` the scalar is
`s • c₀`. This is the toy stand-in for the (Ind3)-choice `S` of [LANA] §9.2 — an element of the group,
not an index into a list. -/
def orbitFamily (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c₀ : ℝ) (s : H) : ℝ := ((s : ℝˣ) : ℝ) * c₀
/-- **Equality of maps is orbit membership.** This is the chain of the task in one statement: there is a
choice in the family whose map equals `etaQ q` iff `q` is the image of the base scalar `c₀` under the
indeterminacy. Proof: `exists_eta_eq_iff_exists_scalar` reduces the maps to scalars, and the scaling
relation `q = s • c₀` is the orbit relation — the two directions are the two directions of "membership in
a subgroup". -/
theorem eta_eq_iff_inOrbit (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c₀ q : ℝ) :
(∃ s : H, etaAnab (orbitFamily H c₀) s = etaQ q) ↔ InOrbit H c₀ q := by
rw [exists_eta_eq_iff_exists_scalar]
constructor
· rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
exact ⟨(s : ℝˣ), s.2, hs.symm⟩
· rintro ⟨u, hu, hq⟩
refine ⟨⟨u, hu⟩, ?_⟩
show (u : ℝ) * c₀ = q
exact hq.symm
/-- **(9-1) in the toy, in orbit form**: there is a choice in the family with `η^anab = η_q` iff there is
a choice whose own scalar has `q` in its orbit. This is the statement the task items 3 and 4 ask for; the
right-hand side is *not* a mere restatement, because the family is indexed by the group and the orbit of a
member of the family is the orbit of the base scalar (`eta_eq_iff_inOrbit` closes the circle). -/
theorem in_orbit_iff_exists_iso_in_family (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c₀ q : ℝ) :
(∃ S₀ : H, etaAnab (orbitFamily H c₀) S₀ = etaQ q) ↔
∃ S₀ : H, InOrbit H (orbitFamily H c₀ S₀) q := by
rw [eta_eq_iff_inOrbit]
constructor
· rintro ⟨u, hu, hq⟩
refine ⟨⟨1, H.one_mem⟩, u, hu, ?_⟩
simpa [orbitFamily] using hq
· rintro ⟨s, u, hu, hq⟩
refine ⟨u * (s : ℝˣ), H.mul_mem hu s.2, ?_⟩
rw [Units.val_mul, hq, orbitFamily]
ring
/-- **The constructive direction**: an orbit member produces a choice `S` in the family for which the two
maps coincide. In the toy this is the only thing that would ever discharge (9-1), and it is a statement
about the indeterminacy, not about the maps. -/
theorem exists_S_of_inOrbit (H : Subgroup ℝˣ) (c₀ q : ℝ) (h : InOrbit H c₀ q) :
∃ s : H, etaAnab (orbitFamily H c₀) s = etaQ q :=
(eta_eq_iff_inOrbit H c₀ q).mpr h
/-- **With the whole unit group as indeterminacy, the orbit of a non-zero scalar is every non-zero
scalar.** This is what makes the toy's obstruction sharp: the only scalar that no choice can reach is
`0`, i.e. the collapse case of §2. -/
theorem top_inOrbit_iff (c q : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) : InOrbit ⊤ c q ↔ q ≠ 0 := by
constructor
· rintro ⟨u, -, hq⟩
rw [hq]
exact mul_ne_zero (Units.ne_zero u) hc
· intro hq
refine ⟨Units.mk0 (q / c) (div_ne_zero hq hc), Subgroup.mem_top _, ?_⟩
rw [Units.val_mk0, div_mul_cancel₀ q hc]
/-- **A case where the toy's (9-1) holds, with an explicit choice**: `q = 4` is reached from `c₀ = 1` by
the unit `4`, whose existence is `top_inOrbit_iff`; the choice itself is `Units.mk0 (4 / 1)`. -/
theorem nine_one_at_four : ∃ s : (⊤ : Subgroup ℝˣ), etaAnab (orbitFamily ⊤ 1) s = etaQ 4 :=
exists_S_of_inOrbit ⊤ 1 4 ((top_inOrbit_iff 1 4 one_ne_zero).mpr (by norm_num))
/-- **A case where no choice in the family gives equality, with the whole unit group as indeterminacy**:
the target scalar `0` is not in the orbit of `1`, because every unit is non-zero. The target map `etaQ 0`
is the zero map (`etaQ_apply`), so its own pilot is zero and it is not an isomorphism. -/
theorem no_S_top_zero : ¬ ∃ s : (⊤ : Subgroup ℝˣ), etaAnab (orbitFamily ⊤ 1) s = etaQ 0 := by
rintro h
have h' : InOrbit ⊤ (1 : ℝ) 0 := (eta_eq_iff_inOrbit ⊤ 1 0).mp h
exact ((top_inOrbit_iff 1 0 one_ne_zero).mp h') rfl
/-! ## 4. Degeneracy, both directions, with numbers -/
/-- **The identity map of the pointed line**: multiplication by `1`. -/
def idMap : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss := scalarMap 1
/-- **Multiplication by `2`**: a second map of the same pointed line, different from `idMap`. -/
def doubleMap : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss := scalarMap 2
/-- `idMap` kills `0`, as every linear map does. -/
theorem idMap_zero : idMap 0 = 0 := by
rw [idMap, scalarMap_apply, mul_zero]
/-- `doubleMap` kills `0` as well. -/
theorem doubleMap_zero : doubleMap 0 = 0 := by
rw [doubleMap, scalarMap_apply, mul_zero]
/-- **The two maps are different**: they disagree at `1`, where the values are `1` and `2`. -/
theorem idMap_ne_doubleMap : idMap ≠ doubleMap := by
intro h
have h1 : idMap 1 = doubleMap 1 := LinearMap.congr_fun h 1
rw [idMap, doubleMap, scalarMap_apply, scalarMap_apply] at h1
norm_num at h1
/-- **Agreement at a zero pilot does not determine a map of pointed lines**: `idMap ≠ doubleMap` while
`idMap 0 = 0 = doubleMap 0`. This is why `map_eq_iff_pilot` carries `p ≠ 0`, and it is the toy form of the
reason `ValBPS.eta_eq_eta_iff` is a statement about a *non-zero* pilot point. -/
theorem agreement_at_zero_not_determining :
∃ f g : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss, f ≠ g ∧ f 0 = g 0 :=
⟨idMap, doubleMap, idMap_ne_doubleMap, by rw [idMap_zero, doubleMap_zero]⟩
/-- **Without the hypothesis `p ≠ 0` the reduction lemma is false**, stated as the sharp negation: it is
not the case that agreement at `0` forces equality of maps. -/
theorem zero_pilot_not_determining : ¬ ∀ f g : Rval →ₗ[ℝ] Rss, f 0 = g 0 → f = g := by
intro h
exact idMap_ne_doubleMap (h idMap doubleMap (by rw [idMap_zero, doubleMap_zero]))
/-- **`map_eq_iff_pilot` at `p = 0` is false**, for the two maps above: `idMap ≠ doubleMap` while
`idMap 0 = doubleMap 0`, so the equivalence fails at the zero pilot. -/
theorem map_eq_iff_pilot_fails_at_zero : ¬ (idMap = doubleMap ↔ idMap 0 = doubleMap 0) := by
rw [idMap_zero, doubleMap_zero]
simp [idMap_ne_doubleMap]
/-- **With the trivial indeterminacy the family is a single map.** At the only index, `s • c₀ = c₀`, so
the family collapses to `scalarMap c₀`. -/
theorem orbitFamily_bot (c₀ : ℝ) (s : (⊥ : Subgroup ℝˣ)) : orbitFamily ⊥ c₀ s = c₀ := by
obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := s
have hu1 : u = 1 := Subgroup.mem_bot.mp hu
subst hu1
simp [orbitFamily]
/-- **The failure at `H = ⊥`, exhibited at the pilot**: every member of the trivial family sends `1` to
`1`, while `etaQ 2` sends it to `2`. Both maps are isomorphisms of pointed lines
(`etaAnab_bijective`, `etaQ_bijective`), so this is a failure of orbit membership and not a collapse. -/
theorem bottom_pointwise (s : (⊥ : Subgroup ℝˣ)) :
etaAnab (orbitFamily ⊥ 1) s 1 = 1 ∧ etaQ 2 1 = 2 := by
constructor
· rw [etaAnab_apply, orbitFamily_bot, mul_one]
· rw [etaQ_apply, mul_one]
/-- **`2` is not in the orbit of `1` under the trivial indeterminacy**: the scalar fact behind the failure
below, proved on its own so that "the scalar equation has no solution" is a theorem and not an inference
from the maps. -/
theorem not_inOrbit_bot : ¬ InOrbit (⊥ : Subgroup ℝˣ) (1 : ℝ) 2 := by
rintro ⟨u, hu, hq⟩
rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hu
subst hu
rw [Units.val_one, one_mul] at hq
norm_num at hq
/-- **No choice in the trivial family gives equality at `q = 2`.** The family's only scalar is `1`, the
target scalar is `2`, and `2` is not in its orbit (`not_inOrbit_bot`): the scalar equation of §2 has no
solution, so by `exists_eta_eq_iff_exists_scalar` neither does the equation of maps. Numbers: `1` against
theorem no_S_below_bottom : ¬ ∃ s : (⊥ : Subgroup ℝˣ), etaAnab (orbitFamily ⊥ 1) s = etaQ 2 := by
rintro ⟨s, h⟩
have h1 : etaAnab (orbitFamily ⊥ 1) s 1 = etaQ 2 1 := LinearMap.congr_fun h 1
rw [etaAnab_apply, orbitFamily_bot, etaQ_apply] at h1
norm_num at h1
end
end EtaComparison

# W12 toy: the label-indexed normalization and the orbit average coincide exactly when the labels are the
orbit
**Scope.** This file formalises one algebraic identity, one corollary of it, and one concrete failure of
the identity once its hypothesis is dropped. The carrier is a finite label set `Lab`, a finite group `G`
acting on `Lab` through a `MulAction`, a base label `base : Lab`, and readings `f : Lab → ℚ_[3]`. Nothing
else is formalised: no topology, no logarithm series, no norm, no structure beyond `Fintype`, `Group`,
`MulAction` and the commutative field `ℚ_[3]`.
**The two normalizations.** The source normalises a reading in two places in two syntactically different
ways. In the procession normalization of IUT III, Step (x) (txt 10904–10922) the average is taken over
`j ∈ F_l^⋆`, a *group*. In (xi-d) (txt 11022) the log-volume is indexed by `j ∈ |F_l|`, a *label set*. The
two are:
* `averageOverLabels f = (∑ l : Lab, f l) / (card Lab)` — the `|F_l|`-indexed normalization;
* `averageOverOrbit G base f = (∑ g : G, f (g • base)) / (card G)` — the `F_l^⋆`-average along the orbit of
the base label.
**The hypothesis, and how it is encoded.** The source's alignment (IUT II, Corollary 4.10, (i), txt
7003–7010) identifies the collections of data `Ψcns(F)_0` and `Ψcns(F)_{⟨F_l^⋆⟩}`, i.e. it says the label
`0` *is* the orbit `⟨F_l^⋆⟩`. The hypothesis that turns that slogan into mathematics is **simple
transitivity through `base`**: the map `g ↦ g • base` is a bijection `G → Lab`, encoded as the hypothesis
`hAct : Function.Bijective (fun g : G => g • base)` on the given `MulAction`. This is the statement that
the labels are the orbit — each label is `g • base` for exactly one `g`, so there are exactly as many
labels as group elements and each label is hit once. It is stated as a hypothesis rather than as a
structure, so that the anti-degeneracy below can drop it and keep the same definitions.
**What is proved, in order.**
* `averageOverLabels`, `averageOverOrbit` — the two normalizations, both in `ℚ_[3]`. `G` is an explicit
argument of `averageOverOrbit` because it does not occur in the type of the reading (a reading is a
function on the label set), so it has to be said which group is being averaged over.
* `InvariantReading` — the hypothesis "the reading does not see which representative of the orbit is
used", `f (a • l) = f l`.
* `card_eq_card_of_bijective` — the two denominator cardinalities agree, by `Fintype.card_congr` applied
to `Equiv.ofBijective`.
* `sum_over_labels_eq_sum_over_orbit` — the numerators agree: the sum over the label set is the sum over
the group indexed along the orbit. This is the reindexing step (`Fintype.sum_bijective`, the `Finset`
version cited by the task), and it needs no invariance.
* `averageOverLabels_eq_averageOverOrbit` — **the deliverable identity**: under `hAct`, the two
normalizations are equal for *every* reading. Note what this does and does not use: numerator equality is
pure reindexing, denominator equality is `card_congr`, and no property of the reading enters. The
identity is therefore a statement about the *indexings*, not about the reading — which is exactly the
content of "the labels are the orbit".
* `card_cast_ne_zero`, `sum_orbit_eq_card_mul`, `averageOverOrbit_eq_base_of_invariant`, `coord_at_base`
— the W5 result recovered here as a corollary of the identity: for an invariant reading, averaging (over
the labels, and over the orbit) is evaluation at the base label.
* **Anti-degeneracy (item 5)**: `ToyLab := ZMod 3` (three labels), `ToyGroup := (ZMod 3)ˣ` (the two units,
acting by multiplication), base label `0`. This is the smallest faithful shape of "the labels are not
the orbit": the units swap the labels `1` and `2` and fix `0`, so the orbit of `0` is `{0}`, a proper
subset of the three labels. Then `toyGroup_card` is `2` while `toyLab_card` is `3`, `toy_not_bijective`
says `g ↦ g • 0` is not a bijection (so `hAct` genuinely fails), and for the concrete reading
`toyReading` with values `1, 2, 3` at the labels `0, 1, 2` the two normalizations are computed:
`averageOverLabels_toyReading` gives `(1 + 2 + 3) / 3 = 2`, `averageOverOrbit_toyReading` gives
`(1 + 1) / 2 = 1`, and `toy_averages_differ` separates them, `2 ≠ 1`. The two numbers are computed, not
asserted, and `averageOverOrbit_eq_value_at_base` records that the orbit average is the value at the
base label here — the orbit side is exact because `0` is fixed; it is the label side that fails.
**What this file does not say.** It is a toy, and the following are outside it.
1. It does **not** identify the source's `|F_l|` with `F_l^⋆`. Whether (xi-d)'s index `j ∈ |F_l|` is the
same convention as the `F_l^⋆`-average of Step (x) is a *definition alignment* in the source
(`research/core-backward-2026-10-23/h3-prerequisites.md`, §M-iii, item 1 of 要补的证明), supported by
IUT II, Corollary 4.10, (i) and IUT III, txt 10917–10922. What is proved here is the conditional: **if**
the labels are the orbit **then** the two indexings give the same number, and **if** they are not (the
anti-degeneracy) **then** they can differ. That is a statement about when such an identification would
be forced, not an identification.
2. It does not say the identification holds in the source's setting. In the anti-degeneracy, the labels
are `ZMod 3` and the group is its unit group; that is a toy model of "a group acting on a label set with
a fixed label", not the label group of a number field.
3. No procession, capsule, theta value, theta-link, `F_l^⋆`, `|F_l|`, `⟨F_l^⋆⟩`, F-prime-strip,
Frobenioid, log-volume, log-shell, Hodge theater, coricity, poly-isomorphism, `Ism` or `Ind1`/`Ind2`/
`Ind3` occurs in this file. In particular the file says nothing about (Ind1)–(Ind3), so it does not
reproduce the source's claim that the procession-normalized volume is invariant under (Ind1), (Ind2) and
bounded under (Ind3); that claim is not touched.
4. It says nothing about `ℚ_[3]` beyond its commutative field structure: the norm, the valuation, the
logarithm series and the principal-unit bounds of the other provinces do not occur here. `ℚ_[3]` is used
only because it is the field in which the earlier provinces read their log-volumes, so the two averages
are stated in the same ring; nothing here depends on `3` being prime beyond the field structure.
5. It is not evidence for or against any IUT claim. The core GAP of
`research/core-backward-2026-10-23/h3-prerequisites.md` stays OPEN: `M`-uniqueness (M-i, M-ii) and the
two unwritten normalizations (M-iii) are untouched, and item 1 above is precisely the obligation this
file does *not* discharge.
6. The identity `averageOverLabels_eq_averageOverOrbit` is deliberately weak in one direction: because no
property of the reading enters it, it must not be quoted as an averaging theorem with analytic content.
Its whole content is that a bijective orbit map lets a sum over labels be rewritten as a sum over the
group. The corollary `coord_at_base` is where invariance enters, and there the hypothesis is strong:
invariance forces the reading to be constant on the orbit, so the average collapses to the value at
`base` rather than being computed from non-constant data.
**Why nothing is imported from the other toy files.** `NormalizationAlignment.lean`,
`ReadingInvariance.lean`, `TransitionCompatibility.lean` and the remaining toy files are top-level modules
of this directory, not modules of the package: `lakefile.lean` declares a single library, `lean_lib
CoreTransport`, whose modules are the ones under `CoreTransport/`, so those files are not Lake targets, no
`olean` of them exists and none is importable. Nothing from them is needed: the two normalizations and the
invariance hypothesis are restated here from scratch (they are three definitions and are cheaper to
restate than to depend on), and the only import is `CoreLog.QpThree`, which supplies the notation `ℚ_[3]`
and Mathlib's field structure on it.
A dependency-footprint block at the end of the file records, for every declaration below, that its only
dependencies are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
namespace LabelNormalization
noncomputable section
/-! ## 1. The two normalizations of a reading -/
/-- **The `|F_l|`-indexed normalization**: the reading is summed over the label set and divided by the
number of labels. This is the shape of (xi-d) (IUT III, txt 11022), "suitably normalized, with respect to
`j ∈ |F_l|`", with the labels playing the role of `|F_l|`. The division is by `card Lab` cast to `ℚ_[3]`;
`card_cast_ne_zero` below is the nonzero-ness that the cancellation in `coord_at_base` consumes. -/
def averageOverLabels {Lab : Type*} [Fintype Lab] (f : Lab → ℚ_[3]) : ℚ_[3] :=
(∑ l : Lab, f l) / (Fintype.card Lab : ℚ_[3])
/-- **The `F_l^⋆`-average**: the reading is summed over the group `G` along the orbit of a base label, and
divided by the number of group elements. This is the shape of the procession normalization of IUT III,
Step (x) (txt 10904–10922): "the average is taken over `j ∈ F_l^⋆`". The base label `base` stands for the
label `0` which IUT II, Corollary 4.10, (i) identifies with `⟨F_l^⋆⟩`. The group `G` is an explicit
argument: it does not occur in the type of the reading, so nothing else could determine it. -/
def averageOverOrbit (G : Type*) [Group G] {Lab : Type*} [Fintype G] [MulAction G Lab]
(base : Lab) (f : Lab → ℚ_[3]) : ℚ_[3] :=
(∑ g : G, f (g • base)) / (Fintype.card G : ℚ_[3])
/-! ## 2. Invariance of the reading under the label action
`G` is an explicit argument of the definition for the same reason as in `averageOverOrbit`. -/
/-- **The reading is invariant under the label action**: it gives the same value at `a • l` as at `l`, i.e.
it does not see which representative of the orbit is used. This is the hypothesis of
`sum_orbit_eq_card_mul`, `averageOverOrbit_eq_base_of_invariant` and `coord_at_base`. -/
def InvariantReading (G : Type*) [Group G] {Lab : Type*} [MulAction G Lab]
(f : Lab → ℚ_[3]) : Prop :=
∀ (a : G) (l : Lab), f (a • l) = f l
/-! ## 3. The identity: the two normalizations coincide when the labels are the orbit -/
section Reindexing
variable {Lab : Type*} [Fintype Lab] {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [MulAction G Lab]
(base : Lab)
/-- **The denominators agree**: the label set and the group have the same number of elements, because
`g ↦ g • base` is a bijection. This is the `Fintype.card_congr` half of the identity, and it is where
"there are as many labels as group elements" is used. -/
theorem card_eq_card_of_bijective (hAct : Function.Bijective (fun g : G => g • base)) :
Fintype.card G = Fintype.card Lab :=
Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.ofBijective (fun g : G => g • base) hAct)
/-- **The numerators agree**: the sum over the label set is the sum over the group taken along the orbit.
This is a pure change of indexing variables along the bijection `g ↦ g • base` — the `Finset.sum_bijective`
step of the task — and it uses no property of the reading whatever. -/
theorem sum_over_labels_eq_sum_over_orbit
(hAct : Function.Bijective (fun g : G => g • base)) (f : Lab → ℚ_[3]) :
∑ l : Lab, f l = ∑ g : G, f (g • base) :=
(Fintype.sum_bijective (fun g : G => g • base) hAct (fun g => f (g • base)) f
(fun _ => rfl)).symm
/-- **The deliverable identity.** If the labels are the orbit — `g ↦ g • base` bijective — then the
`|F_l|`-indexed normalization and the `F_l^⋆`-average agree, for **every** reading, invariant or not: the
numerators agree by reindexing (`sum_over_labels_eq_sum_over_orbit`) and the denominators by
`card_eq_card_of_bijective`. Nothing about `f` is used, which is why the identity is a statement about the
indexings rather than about the reading. -/
theorem averageOverLabels_eq_averageOverOrbit
(hAct : Function.Bijective (fun g : G => g • base)) (f : Lab → ℚ_[3]) :
averageOverLabels f = averageOverOrbit G base f := by
unfold averageOverLabels averageOverOrbit
rw [sum_over_labels_eq_sum_over_orbit base hAct f, card_eq_card_of_bijective base hAct]
end Reindexing
/-! ## 4. The W5 result as a corollary: for an invariant reading, averaging is evaluation at `base` -/
section InvariantAverages
variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] {Lab : Type*} [MulAction G Lab]
/-- The number of group elements, cast to `ℚ_[3]`, is nonzero. This is the hypothesis the division needs;
it holds because a group is nonempty. -/
theorem card_cast_ne_zero : ((Fintype.card G : ℕ) : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0 := by
rw [Nat.cast_ne_zero]
exact Fintype.card_ne_zero
/-- **Under invariance the orbit sum is the cardinality times the value at the base label**: every summand
`f (g • base)` equals `f base`, so the sum is `card G` copies of it. -/
theorem sum_orbit_eq_card_mul (base : Lab) {f : Lab → ℚ_[3]} (hInv : InvariantReading G f) :
∑ g : G, f (g • base) = (Fintype.card G : ℚ_[3]) * f base := by
rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun g (_ : g ∈ Finset.univ) => hInv g base), Finset.sum_const,
Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
/-- **The orbit average of an invariant reading is the value at the base label** — the W5 statement
`average_eq_value_of_invariant`, with the base label in place of its label `1`. The hypothesis `hAct` is
*not* needed for this half: the orbit average is exact as soon as the reading is constant on the orbit,
whether or not the orbit exhausts the label set. This asymmetry with `coord_at_base` is the point of the
anti-degeneracy in §5. -/
theorem averageOverOrbit_eq_base_of_invariant (base : Lab) {f : Lab → ℚ_[3]}
(hInv : InvariantReading G f) : averageOverOrbit G base f = f base := by
rw [averageOverOrbit, sum_orbit_eq_card_mul base hInv,
mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ (card_cast_ne_zero (G := G))]
end InvariantAverages
section Coordinate
variable {Lab : Type*} [Fintype Lab] {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [MulAction G Lab]
/-- **The label average of an invariant reading is the value at the base label (item 4 of the task).** This
is the W5 result recovered as a corollary of `averageOverLabels_eq_averageOverOrbit`: reindexing turns the
label average into the orbit average, and invariance turns the orbit average into the value at `base`. The
identification "label `0` ↔ orbit `⟨F_l^⋆⟩`" does its work here: it is what allows the label `base` to be
read off the group average. -/
theorem coord_at_base (base : Lab) (hAct : Function.Bijective (fun g : G => g • base))
{f : Lab → ℚ_[3]} (hInv : InvariantReading G f) : averageOverLabels f = f base := by
rw [averageOverLabels_eq_averageOverOrbit base hAct f,
averageOverOrbit_eq_base_of_invariant base hInv]
end Coordinate
/-! ## 5. Anti-degeneracy: labels that are not the orbit, with the two averages computed
The label set is `ZMod 3` (three labels) and the group is its unit group, which has two elements and acts by
multiplication. The units swap the labels `1` and `2` and fix `0`, so the orbit of the base label `0` is
`{0}`: the labels are *not* the orbit, `g ↦ g • 0` is not injective, and `hAct` fails. For the reading
`1, 2, 3` the label average is `(1 + 2 + 3) / 3 = 2` while the orbit average is `(1 + 1) / 2 = 1`; the two
numbers are computed below and separated by `2 ≠ 1`. -/
section AntiDegeneracy
/-- The toy label set of the anti-degeneracy: three labels, standing for `|F_l|`. -/
abbrev ToyLab : Type := ZMod 3
/-- The toy group of the anti-degeneracy: the two units of `ZMod 3`, standing for `F_l^⋆`, acting on the
labels by multiplication. -/
abbrev ToyGroup : Type := (ZMod 3)ˣ
/-- Three labels. -/
theorem toyLab_card : Fintype.card ToyLab = 3 := ZMod.card 3
/-- Two group elements. -/
theorem toyGroup_card : Fintype.card ToyGroup = 2 := by decide
/-- The base label is fixed by the whole group: `0` is absorbing for multiplication. This is why the orbit
of `0` is the single label `{0}`, and it is also why the orbit sum below is two copies of `f 0`. -/
theorem toy_smul_zero (u : ToyGroup) : u • (0 : ToyLab) = 0 := by simp
/-- The three labels, enumerated. -/
theorem toy_univ : (Finset.univ : Finset ToyLab) = {0, 1, 2} := by decide
/-- The labels are distinct; these three facts are what let the sums below be evaluated rather than left as
`Finset.sum` expressions. -/
theorem toy_zero_ne_one : (0 : ToyLab) ≠ 1 := by decide
theorem toy_zero_ne_two : (0 : ToyLab) ≠ 2 := by decide
theorem toy_one_ne_two : (1 : ToyLab) ≠ 2 := by decide
/-- **The concrete reading**: `1` at the label `0`, `2` at the label `1`, `3` at the label `2`. -/
def toyReading (x : ToyLab) : ℚ_[3] := if x = 0 then 1 else if x = 1 then 2 else 3
/-- The reading at the base label. -/
theorem toyReading_zero : toyReading 0 = 1 := by simp [toyReading]
theorem toyReading_one : toyReading 1 = 2 := by
have h : (1 : ToyLab) ≠ 0 := toy_zero_ne_one.symm
simp [toyReading, h]
theorem toyReading_two : toyReading 2 = 3 := by
have h0 : (2 : ToyLab) ≠ 0 := toy_zero_ne_two.symm
have h1 : (2 : ToyLab) ≠ 1 := toy_one_ne_two.symm
simp [toyReading, h0, h1]
/-- **The label sum, computed**: `1 + 2 + 3 = 6`. The sum over the three labels is expanded along the
enumeration `toy_univ`, and the reading is evaluated at each label. -/
theorem toyReading_sum : ∑ x : ToyLab, toyReading x = 6 := by
rw [toy_univ, Finset.sum_insert (by decide), Finset.sum_pair toy_one_ne_two, toyReading_zero,
toyReading_one, toyReading_two]
norm_num
/-- **The orbit sum, computed**: both group elements fix the base label `0`, so the sum is `f 0 + f 0 = 2`,
and the division by `card G = 2` returns `f 0 = 1`. -/
theorem toyOrbit_sum : ∑ u : ToyGroup, toyReading (u • (0 : ToyLab)) = 2 := by
calc ∑ u : ToyGroup, toyReading (u • (0 : ToyLab))
= ∑ _u : ToyGroup, toyReading (0 : ToyLab) :=
Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun u _ => by rw [toy_smul_zero])
rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, toyGroup_card, nsmul_eq_mul, toyReading_zero,
mul_one]
norm_num
/-- **The `|F_l|`-indexed normalization of the concrete reading is `2`**: `6 / 3`. -/
theorem averageOverLabels_toyReading :
averageOverLabels (fun x : ToyLab => toyReading x) = 2 := by
unfold averageOverLabels
rw [toyReading_sum, toyLab_card]
rw [div_eq_iff (by norm_num : ((3 : ℕ) : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0)]
norm_num
/-- **The `F_l^⋆`-average of the concrete reading is `1`**: `2 / 2`. -/
theorem averageOverOrbit_toyReading :
averageOverOrbit ToyGroup (0 : ToyLab) toyReading = 1 := by
unfold averageOverOrbit
rw [toyOrbit_sum, toyGroup_card]
rw [div_eq_iff (by norm_num : ((2 : ℕ) : ℚ_[3]) ≠ 0)]
norm_num
/-- The orbit average is the value at the base label here — the orbit half of §4 survives without `hAct`,
because the base label is fixed. It is the label half that fails, which is the content of
`toy_averages_differ`. -/
theorem averageOverOrbit_eq_value_at_base :
averageOverOrbit ToyGroup (0 : ToyLab) toyReading = toyReading 0 := by
rw [averageOverOrbit_toyReading, toyReading_zero]
/-- **The hypothesis of the main theorem genuinely fails here**: `g ↦ g • 0` is not injective, so it is not
a bijection of the two-element group onto the three labels. Equivalently, `2 ≠ 3`. -/
theorem toy_not_bijective : ¬ Function.Bijective (fun u : ToyGroup => u • (0 : ToyLab)) := by
intro h
have hc := card_eq_card_of_bijective (G := ToyGroup) (base := (0 : ToyLab)) h
rw [toyGroup_card, toyLab_card] at hc
exact absurd hc (by norm_num)
/-- **The anti-degeneracy (item 5 of the task), as computed numbers**: without `hAct` the two
normalizations differ — the label average is `2`, the orbit average is `1`. A concrete `≠` between two
computed values, not a negated universal. -/
theorem toy_averages_differ :
averageOverLabels (fun x : ToyLab => toyReading x) ≠
averageOverOrbit ToyGroup (0 : ToyLab) toyReading := by
rw [averageOverLabels_toyReading, averageOverOrbit_toyReading]
norm_num
end AntiDegeneracy
end
end LabelNormalization

import CoreLog.QpThree
# Delegated log bridge: two literal logarithms, one series
`CoreTransport.localLog` and `PadicLogVolume.padicLog` are two independently written literal
logarithm series. This file connects them on the actual `ℚ_[3]`, and then feeds the existing
`Q_3` convergence result into the transport tool's own logarithm.
What this file is, and is not:
* Item 1 is **definition-level wiring**, not mathematical content. The two series have the same
term `(-1)^n (x-1)^{n+1}/(n+1)`; the theorem records that fact in the open, with both
definitions unfolded, so that no later claim rests on them being secretly different objects.
* Item 2 genuinely consumes the convergence proof (`CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable`) — the
`HasSum` statement is derived from summability, not read off `tsum`'s junk default value.
* Item 3 transports the closed-ball image statement through item 1.
* Nothing here constructs a Θ-link, an `Ism`, or anything belonging to IUT; no Galois or
deformation structure is added, and no new instance is introduced.
namespace DelegatedLogBridge
noncomputable section
open Filter Topology
/-- **Item 1 (definition-level wiring).** On the actual `ℚ_[3]` the transport tool's logarithm
and the `Q_3` logarithm are the same series, term for term. Both definitions are unfolded here:
this is an identification of two existing definitions, not a new function. -/
theorem localLog_eq_padicLog (x : ℚ_[3]) :
CoreTransport.localLog x = PadicLogVolume.padicLog x := by
unfold CoreTransport.localLog PadicLogVolume.padicLog PadicLogVolume.logTerm
rfl
/-- **Item 2a.** The same series is summable on the principal units of `ℚ_[3]`, quoting the
existing `Q_3` convergence result rather than re-proving it. -/
theorem summable_logTerm {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
Summable (PadicLogVolume.logTerm x) :=
CoreLog.principal_unit_log_summable hx
/-- **Item 2b.** For `‖x - 1‖ < 1` the series sums to `CoreTransport.localLog x`. The proof goes
through summability (`summable_logTerm`), so it depends on the actual convergence argument and
not on the totalized `tsum` default. -/
theorem hasSum_logTerm_localLog {x : ℚ_[3]} (hx : ‖x - 1‖ < 1) :
HasSum (PadicLogVolume.logTerm x) (CoreTransport.localLog x) := by
rw [localLog_eq_padicLog x]
exact (summable_logTerm hx).hasSum
/-- **Item 3.** The transport tool's log image of the principal units of `ℚ_[3]` is exactly the
closed ball of radius `‖3‖ = 1/3`. Derived from the existing closed-ball statement by rewriting
along item 1 only. -/
theorem logImage_Q3_eq_closedBall :
CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3] = {y : ℚ_[3] | ‖y‖ ≤ (3 : ℝ)⁻¹} := by
have h : CoreTransport.logImage ℚ_[3]
= PadicLogVolume.padicLog '' {u : ℚ_[3] | ‖u - 1‖ < 1} := by
unfold CoreTransport.logImage
have hfun : (CoreTransport.localLog : ℚ_[3] → ℚ_[3]) = PadicLogVolume.padicLog := by
funext u
exact localLog_eq_padicLog u
rw [hfun]
rw [h, CoreLog.principal_unit_log_image]
end
end DelegatedLogBridge
